families.placement: What goes in which directory and how files are named (suffixes, segments, extensions, source roots).
families.convention-files: What a file in a convention directory (routes/, middleware/, crons/, queues/, email/, durable-objects/, db/, auth.ts, env.ts, SSR entry) must export.
families.imports: Which module an API comes from (void/*, adapter packages, drizzle, better-auth) and which modules may not be imported.
families.server-client-boundary: Server-only modules and secrets must not reach browser code, and client-only modules must not reach server code.
families.handlers: defineHandler, withValidator, defineMiddleware helpers, basicAuth, HTTPException and Hono middleware usage in handlers.
families.pages: Pages routing: loaders, actions, .server companions, props, prerender paths, Link, router, layouts, error pages, adapter specifics.
families.forms-actions: useForm, action(), island forms and file uploads in actions.
families.head: head() / defineHead, titleTemplate, headDefaults, social images.
families.islands: Island pages and the island import attribute.
families.typed-urls: routeUrl, Href/RouteUrl types, typedRoutes-related code, redirects and rewrites targets.
families.typed-fetch: fetch from void/client: path, params, query, method and body.
families.auth: Void-managed Better Auth: auth.ts, requireAuth, caching of user pages, rate-limit headers.
families.env: env.ts, void/env, VITE_ variables and secrets.
families.database: db from void/db, sessions and bookmarks, schema, seeds, D1 replication.
families.resources: kv, storage, ai, sandbox, queues, email, logging, usage limits.
families.realtime: WebSocket rooms, live streams, SSE and durable state.
families.config: void.config.ts and vite.config.ts: options, plugins, literals.
families.edge: Headers, redirects, rewrites, ISR revalidation, prerender settings and static-asset caching.
families.frameworks: Meta-framework integrations (Nuxt, Astro, SvelteKit, React Router, TanStack Start, Analog).
families.platform: Void platform API calls and CI credentials.

rules.name: cron-file-placement
rules.summary: A file that defines a scheduled job sits in crons/.
rules.files: any file calling defineScheduled or exporting `cron`
rules.detect: CallExpression `defineScheduled(...)` or `export const cron` in a file that is not under crons/ (no `_` segment), or whose extension is .tsx/.jsx.

rules.name: durable-object-class-placement
rules.summary: A native Durable Object class lives in its own module under durable-objects/ and is wrapped with defineDurableObject and default-exported.
rules.files: any file declaring `class X extends DurableObject` (or Agent)
rules.detect: ClassDeclaration/ClassExpression whose superclass is `DurableObject` or `Agent`: report when the file is not under durable-objects/, or when it has no `defineDurableObject(...)` call or no `export default`.
reported:
// lib/room.ts
export class Room extends DurableObject {}

// durable-objects/room.ts
export class Room extends DurableObject {}
rules.partial: A class re-exported from another module is not seen.

rules.name: env-suffix-placement
rules.summary: The .dev/.prod suffix is used only on routes and pages, before .island/.ws, and never on layouts or in middleware/, crons/, queues/.
rules.files: middleware/**, crons/**, queues/** (not _-prefixed); pages/** and routes/**; pages/**/layout.* and pages/**/_layouts/**
rules.detect: (1) File name matches /\.(dev|prod)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/ under one of the three directories. (2) File name matches /\.(island|ws)\.(dev|prod)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/. (3) File is named `layout.dev.*` or `layout.prod.*`, or sits in a `_layouts/` directory and has `.dev.` or `.prod.` in its name.
allowed:
// middleware/01.logger.ts
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => next());

// pages/layout.tsx
export default function Layout({ children }) { return children; }
reported:
// middleware/01.logger.dev.ts
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => next());

// pages/layout.dev.tsx
export default function Layout({ children }) { return children; }

rules.name: no-conventions-outside-source-dir
rules.summary: With `sourceDir` set, convention directories and auth.ts/env.ts live under it, not at the project root, and never in both places.
rules.files: files at the app root under routes/, pages/, middleware/, crons/, queues/, db/, email/, durable-objects/, plus root auth.ts and env.ts
rules.detect: Only when `settings.void.sourceDir` is set: a file whose path relative to the app root starts with one of those directory names (or is auth.ts / env.ts) and does not start with the sourceDir. Reports the Program. `locate()` already returns null for such files, so the rule needs the root-relative path as a second helper.
rules.partial: Whether the same directory exists under both roots (config/6) is not checked; the rule reports every root-level copy, which is the superset.

rules.name: no-env-file-crossing
rules.summary: A file does not import a .dev module from code that ships to production, nor a .prod module from dev code.
rules.files: routes/** and pages/** (and anything inside them)
rules.detect: ImportDeclaration / dynamic import / export-from with a relative specifier whose last segment (before the extension) ends in `.dev` or `.prod`, in a file whose own name does not carry the same suffix. Link `href` literals are not followed.
rules.partial: A `.dev` helper imported by an ordinary page is reported even when the import is guarded by `import.meta.env.DEV`; Link hrefs and imports through barrels escape.

rules.name: no-public-import
rules.summary: Files in public/ are referenced by root path, never imported as modules.
rules.detect: ImportDeclaration, dynamic import() or require() with a string-literal specifier that contains `/public/` or starts with `public/` or `./public/` or `../public/` and has an asset extension (not .ts/.js).
rules.partial: Vite's own `public/` alias spelled differently (an absolute `/logo.svg` import) is not seen.

rules.name: no-test-in-route-dirs
rules.summary: Test files stay out of routes/ and pages/ (and the other convention directories), where Void would serve them.
rules.files: any *.test.* / *.spec.* file below a convention directory with no `_` segment
rules.detect: Already implemented in plugin/rules/no-test-in-route-dirs.js: the file name is a Vitest-style test name, it sits in routes/ or pages/, and no segment below the directory starts with `_`.
rules.partial: Implemented for routes/ and pages/ only; the norm also names middleware/, crons/ and queues/, which the rule could add (CONVENTION_DIRS already lists them).

rules.name: queue-file-placement
rules.summary: A queue consumer sits in queues/ with a .ts/.mts/.js/.mjs extension and a path that makes a valid Cloudflare queue name.
rules.files: any file calling defineQueue from 'void' or 'void/handler'; queues/** (not _-prefixed)
rules.detect: (1) CallExpression `defineQueue(...)` whose file is not under queues/ (no `_` segment), or whose extension is .tsx/.jsx. (2) Take the path below queues/ without its extension, replace `/` by `-`; report the Program unless it matches /^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?$/ (underscores inside a name, leading or trailing `-`, length over 63).
rules.partial: A queue consumer written with the raw Workers `queue` export instead of defineQueue is not recognised.

rules.name: route-file-name
rules.summary: A routes/ file has a valid script extension (.tsx/.jsx when it holds JSX) and writes dynamic segments as [id] and [...name].
rules.files: routes/** (not _-prefixed); any file name or extension that Void would scan; routes/** and pages/** (every path segment, including the file name without its extension chain)
rules.detect: (1) File sits in routes/ and no segment below it starts with `_` or `.`. Report the Program when the extension is not one of .ts .tsx .js .jsx .mts .mjs (for example .cjs, .cts, .vue), or when the extension is .ts/.js/.mts/.mjs (including .ws.ts) and the tree contains a JSXElement or JSXFragment (report that first node). (2) For a file below routes/ or pages/ (not skipped by `_`), split the path into segments; report the Program when a segment contains `:`, `{`, `}` or starts with `$`, or has the shape `[name...]`, `[*name]` or is exactly `*`.
rules.reports: the Program (bad extension) or the first JSX node; the Program
rules.partial: A .vue or .svelte route is not linted by oxlint at all. Only the path is read; nothing tells the rule that a `$`-prefixed file is meant as a literal name.

rules.name: schema-file-layout
rules.summary: Drizzle tables are defined in db/schema.ts or db/schema/**, and a db/schema.ts with no tables re-exports them.
rules.files: any file calling sqliteTable / pgTable / mysqlTable; db/schema.ts
rules.detect: (1) CallExpression whose callee is `sqliteTable`, `pgTable` or `mysqlTable` (imported from void/schema-d1|pg|mysql) in a file that is not db/schema.ts, db/schema/**, or the same under sourceDir. (2) db/schema.ts (root or sourceDir) that contains no table-builder call and no `export ... from` declaration at all. Named re-exports are accepted.
rules.partial: Test fixtures that build tables on purpose are reported; allow them with a path override. services/database/5's `export *` form is not required by its quote, so named re-exports pass; whether every file under db/schema/ is re-exported needs the directory listing.

rules.name: auth-file-define-auth
rules.summary: defineAuth(...) is called only in auth.ts at the app root, and auth.ts default-exports it.
rules.files: any file calling defineAuth imported from 'void/auth'; auth.ts (app root or sourceDir)
rules.detect: (1) CallExpression `defineAuth(...)` in a file that is not named auth.ts at the app source root. (2) No `export default`, or the default export is not a call to `defineAuth`.
rules.reports: the call; the default export or the Program
rules.partial: Only the file name is checked reliably; root versus sourceDir needs the setting.

rules.name: cron-file-exports
rules.summary: A file in crons/ exports a literal `cron` and default-exports defineScheduled(...); helpers start with `_`.
rules.detect: (1) Program lacks a named export `cron`, or lacks `export default`, or the default export is not a call to `defineScheduled` (imported from 'void' or 'void/handler'). (2) `export const cron = <init>` where init is not a string Literal / no-expression TemplateLiteral, nor an ArrayExpression whose elements are all such literals.
rules.reports: the default export, or the Program; the initialiser
rules.partial: The doc calls defineScheduled 'recommended', so a plain default function is reported only as a lesser finding if the rule has severities. The literal requirement is inferred from how Void reads the export, not stated outright.

rules.name: define-auth-spread-defaults
rules.summary: The object returned from the defineAuth callback spreads `defaults`.
rules.detect: In `defineAuth(cb)`, find the object returned by cb (arrow body or the returned ObjectExpression); report when it has no SpreadElement of the identifier destructured as `defaults` from cb's first parameter (or `ctx.defaults`).
allowed:
// auth.ts
export default defineAuth(({ defaults }) => ({ ...defaults, plugins: [] }));
reported:
// auth.ts
export default defineAuth(({ defaults }) => ({ plugins: [] }));
rules.partial: A returned identifier or a call result is not followed.

rules.name: durable-state-module
rules.summary: defineDurableState() is called only in durable-objects/ modules, which default-export it (and also export it by name).
rules.files: any file calling defineDurableState or defineDurableObject; durable-objects/** (not _-prefixed); durable-objects/**
rules.detect: (1) CallExpression `defineDurableState(...)` / `defineDurableObject(...)` (imported from 'void/durable') in a file not under durable-objects/ (no `_` segment). (2) No `export default`, or its value (following one same-file identifier) is not a call to `defineDurableState` / `defineDurableObject`. (3) A default-exported `defineDurableState` result that is a same-file const with no named export of that const.
rules.reports: the call; the default export or the Program; the default export
reported:
// durable-objects/cart.ts
export const cart = defineDurableState({ name: 'cart' });
rules.partial: Whether any other module needs the RPC import is invisible, so a module nobody calls is reported; keep this rule at warning level.

rules.name: email-handler-file
rules.summary: An inbound email handler is a flat file in the top-level email/ directory whose default export is defineEmail(...).
rules.files: any file calling defineEmail from 'void/email'; email/** (not _-prefixed); email/* (not _-prefixed)
rules.detect: (1) CallExpression `defineEmail(...)` in a file that is not under email/. (2) File path below email/ has more than one segment and no segment starts with `_`. (3) No `export default`, or the default export is not a call to `defineEmail` (from 'void/email').
rules.reports: the call; the Program; the default export or the Program
allowed:
// email/support.ts
export default defineEmail(async (message, env, ctx) => {});

rules.name: env-file-define-env
rules.summary: env.ts at the app root default-exports defineEnv(...) from 'void/env', and defineEnv is called nowhere else.
rules.files: env.ts (app root or sourceDir), any file calling defineEnv
rules.detect: env.ts with no `export default`, or a default export that is not a defineEnv call; a `defineEnv(...)` call in any file not named env.ts.
rules.reports: the default export, the Program or the call
allowed:
// env.ts
export default defineEnv({ API_KEY: z.string() });
reported:
// env.ts
export const env = defineEnv({ API_KEY: z.string() });

rules.name: middleware-default-export
rules.summary: A file in middleware/ default-exports defineMiddleware(...) (or basicAuth(...), which the docs also default-export there).
rules.detect: Program has no `export default`, or its default export is not a call to `defineMiddleware` or `basicAuth` (imported from 'void' or 'void/handler'). A default-exported identifier is followed to a const initialised by such a call in the same file. Named middleware exports are reported only through the missing default.
rules.reports: the default export, or the Program when there is none
allowed:
// middleware/01.logger.ts
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { await next(); });

// middleware/02.gate.ts
export default basicAuth({ username: () => env.U, password: () => env.P });
reported:
// middleware/01.logger.ts
export const mw = defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => next());

// middleware/01.logger.ts
export default async (c, next) => next();
rules.partial: A default export that is an identifier bound elsewhere to a defineMiddleware call is followed; one imported from another module is not. A bare Hono middleware call (`export default cors()`) is a call and is not reported.

rules.name: middleware-numeric-prefix
rules.summary: Global middleware files in middleware/ start with a number (01.logger.ts) that sets their order.
rules.detect: File name does not match /^\d+\./.
allowed:
// middleware/01.logger.ts
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => next());
reported:
// middleware/logger.ts
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => next());

// middleware/auth.ts
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => next());

rules.name: queue-default-export
rules.summary: A file in queues/ default-exports defineQueue<Message>(...); helpers start with `_`.
rules.files: queues/** (not _-prefixed for the first check; _-prefixed for the second); queues/** .ts/.mts files
rules.detect: (1) Non-underscore file under queues/ with no `export default` or whose default export is not a call to `defineQueue`; also a `_`-prefixed file under queues/ that default-exports defineQueue (never registered). (2) CallExpression `defineQueue(...)` with no typeArguments (TypeScript files only); a handler whose `batch` parameter is annotated `QueueBatch<T>` is also accepted.
rules.reports: the default export or the Program; the defineQueue call
rules.partial: Not applicable to .js/.mjs queue files.

rules.name: queue-options
rules.summary: Queue option exports are whole-number literals in the queue file, and maxConcurrency is 1-250.
rules.detect: (1) Exports named maxBatchSize, maxBatchTimeout, maxConcurrency, maxRetries, retryDelay: report unless `export const X = <non-negative integer Literal>`. Report `export { X } from`, `export * from` and `export { y as X }` for those names. (2) `export const maxConcurrency = <integer Literal>` with a value below 1 or above 250.

rules.name: render-includes-asset-tags
rules.summary: A custom SSR renderer inserts assetTags.css and assetTags.preloads in the head and assetTags.body before </body>.
rules.detect: The callback of `defineRender(...)` (or the exported `render`) that has no reference to one of `assetTags.css`, `assetTags.preloads`, `assetTags.body` (member access or destructured from the second parameter).
allowed:
// src/main.ssr.tsx
export default defineRender(async (c, { assetTags: t }) => c.html(t.css + t.preloads + t.body));
reported:
// src/main.ssr.tsx
export default defineRender(async (c, { assetTags }) => c.html(`<head>${assetTags.css}</head>`));
rules.partial: References inside helpers escape.

rules.name: route-handler-define-handler
rules.summary: Each exported HTTP-method handler in routes/ is built with defineHandler (or defineHandler.withValidator(...)(...)).
rules.detect: Export named GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS whose initialiser is not a CallExpression with callee `defineHandler` or `defineHandler.withValidator(...)` (a call of a call). A bare arrow or function is reported; an identifier is followed to its const in the same file.
allowed:
// routes/users.ts
export const POST = defineHandler.withValidator({ body })((c, { body }) => body);
reported:
// routes/users.ts
export const GET = async (c) => c.json([]);

// routes/users.ts
export async function POST(c) { return c.json({}); }
rules.partial: A handler built by a local factory (`makeHandler()`) is reported; one imported from another module is not followed.

rules.name: route-has-handler-export
rules.summary: Every non-underscore file in routes/ exports at least one HTTP-method handler; helpers are prefixed with `_`.
rules.detect: Program with no export named GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS (declaration, specifier or `export * from`). Files with `export *` are skipped.
rules.partial: Directories named with `_` are skipped here because Void skips them; the structure doc only names files.

rules.name: route-no-default-export
rules.summary: A route file exports named HTTP-method handlers (GET, POST, ...), not a default export or lowercase names.
rules.detect: Report an ExportDefaultDeclaration, and any export named `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`, `options` or `handler` (lowercase). Methods recognised: GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE HEAD OPTIONS.

rules.name: seed-module-export
rules.summary: A programmatic seed module exports a default function or a named `seed` function.
rules.files: db/seed.{ts,mts,js,mjs}, and any file importing defineSeed from 'void/seed'
rules.detect: File is db/seed.{ts,mts,js,mjs} (or imports defineSeed): report unless it has `export default <function or defineSeed(...) call>` or `export function seed` / `export const seed = <function>`.

rules.name: ssr-entry-define-render
rules.summary: The custom SSR entry default-exports defineRender(...) or exports a named `render`; scaffolded entries use defineRender.
rules.detect: No default export that is a call to `defineRender`, and no export named `render`.
allowed:
// src/main.ssr.tsx
export default defineRender(async (c, { assetTags }) => c.html(''));

// src/main.ssr.tsx
export const render = async () => new Response('');
rules.partial: A renderer defined in another module and re-exported escapes.

rules.name: ws-route-file
rules.summary: A WebSocket route is a routes/**/*.ws.* file that default-exports defineRoom(...) or defineWebSocket(...).
rules.files: any file calling defineRoom or defineWebSocket from 'void/ws'; routes/**/*.ws.*
rules.detect: (1) CallExpression `defineRoom(...)` / `defineWebSocket(...)`: report when the file is not under routes/ or its name does not match /\.ws\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/. (2) No `export default`, or the default export is not a call to `defineRoom` or `defineWebSocket` (from 'void/ws').
rules.reports: the call; the default export or the Program
reported:
// routes/chat.ws.ts
export const room = defineRoom({ messages });

rules.name: adapter-package-imports
rules.summary: The runtime exports, the Deferred type and the Vite plugin come from the adapter packages (@void/react|vue|svelte|solid and their /plugin).
rules.files: any file; page components and loaders; vite.config.*
rules.detect: (1) ImportDeclaration of Link, useRouter, useParams, useNavigation, useForm, useIslandForm, action, isVoidActionError, isCallSiteActionError, getValidationErrors, useShared or Form from 'void', 'void/pages', 'void/client' or 'void/handler'. (2) Import of `Deferred` from a specifier that is not '@void/react', '@void/vue', '@void/svelte' or '@void/solid'. (3) Import of `voidReact` / `voidVue` / `voidSvelte` / `voidSolid` from a specifier other than '@void/react/plugin', '@void/vue/plugin', '@void/svelte/plugin', '@void/solid/plugin'.
rules.partial: A name that exists in two modules (`auth`, `fetch`) is not in the list.

rules.name: auth-imports-from-void
rules.summary: Auth helpers, the auth client and auth types come from void/auth and void/client; app code builds no Better Auth client or instance.
rules.files: any file; any file except auth.ts; any file except auth.ts and the files it imports
rules.detect: (1) ImportDeclaration importing one of defineAuth/getUser/getSession/getAuth/requireAuth from a specifier other than 'void/auth', or importing `auth` from a specifier other than 'void/client' (or 'void/client/<framework>'). (2) Import of `createAuthClient` from `better-auth/client`, `better-auth/react`, `better-auth/vue`, `better-auth/svelte`, `better-auth/solid` or any specifier other than 'void/client'; or a createAuthClient call whose only option is basePath '/api/auth'. (3) CallExpression whose callee is `betterAuth` imported from 'better-auth'. (4) Import (including `import type`) of `User` or `Session` from 'better-auth' or 'better-auth/types'.
rules.reports: the import specifier; the import specifier or the call; the call
allowed:
import { createAuthClient } from 'void/client';
export const c = createAuthClient({ plugins: [] });
const result = await getAuth(c).api.listSessions({ headers: c.req.raw.headers });
reported:
import { createAuthClient } from 'better-auth/client';
export const c = createAuthClient();

import { betterAuth } from 'better-auth';
export const a = betterAuth({});
rules.partial: An `auth` named import from an unrelated package (for example a local `./auth`) is not reported: only `void`, `void/handler`, `void/pages` and the `@void/*` packages are treated as wrong sources. A custom client with real options is allowed only through 'void/client'. auth.ts itself is exempt, because reference/auth/14 asks for Better Auth's types there.

rules.name: auth-schema-alias
rules.summary: Auth tables are imported from '@auth-schema', never by path into .void/.
rules.detect: Import specifier that contains `.void/better-auth-schema`.

rules.name: no-cloudflare-workers-import
rules.summary: Routes and middleware reach bindings through c.env or the void/* clients, not by importing cloudflare:workers; Nuxt and SvelteKit 2 never import it.
rules.files: routes/** and middleware/** in a native app; any file when the project is Nuxt or SvelteKit 2
rules.detect: Import (static or dynamic) of 'cloudflare:workers' in a file under routes/ or middleware/; or in any file when the project framework is nuxt or sveltekit (package.json dependency `nuxt` or `@sveltejs/kit` ^2, or `settings.void.framework`).
allowed:
// routes/api.ts
export const GET = defineHandler((c) => c.env.DB);
rules.partial: Needs package.json (a lib helper reading it once per root) to know the framework; Astro API routes use cloudflare:workers legitimately and are not covered.

rules.name: no-redefine-auth-tables
rules.summary: db/schema.ts does not redefine Better Auth's user, session, account or verification tables.
rules.detect: Table-builder call (sqliteTable/pgTable/mysqlTable) whose first argument is the literal 'user', 'session', 'account' or 'verification'.
rules.partial: A project that renames Better Auth's model names is not known to the rule.

rules.name: no-resource-import-in-sfc
rules.summary: void/db, void/kv, void/storage, void/ai, void/auth, void/sandbox, void/queues and void/live are not imported from .vue or .svelte files.
rules.detect: Import of those modules in the script block of a .vue or .svelte file.
rules.partial: oxlint lints only the script block of an SFC; template expressions cannot import. Nuxt's wider claim (components/pages outside server/) is covered by nuxt-no-void-in-client.

rules.name: no-undocumented-void-module
rules.summary: Void's APIs are imported only from the paths the docs name as public.
rules.detect: ImportDeclaration, ExportNamedDeclaration/ExportAllDeclaration with source, dynamic import() with a literal, and require() with a literal whose specifier is `void` or starts with `void/` and is not in `norms/reference.json` `publicModules` (shipped with the plugin). Specifiers such as `void/_env` or `void/pages-client` are reported.
rules.partial: Subpaths of a public module that the docs show but the table omits (for example `void/live/client`) must be in publicModules or they are reported.

rules.name: resource-import-in-scanned-dir
rules.summary: Files importing void/db, void/kv, void/storage, void/ai, void/auth, void/sandbox, void/queues or void/live sit in directories Void scans for resources.
rules.files: any file importing one of those modules
rules.detect: File whose first path segment is not one of routes, middleware, queues, pages, crons, email, src, durable-objects (or an entry of the `scanDirs` option, which mirrors inference.scanDirs). The sourceDir setting prefixes the defaults.
options: scanDirs: string[] (default: the documented list), mirrors inference.scanDirs
rules.partial: When the project sets inference.scanDirs in void.config.ts the option must be given too; the rule does not read the config.

rules.name: schema-import-alias
rules.summary: App code imports tables from the @schema alias, not by relative path into db/schema, and gets `db` from 'void/db'.
rules.detect: ImportDeclaration with a relative specifier whose resolved path ends in `db/schema` or `db/schema/<file>` (extension optional), in a file that is not under db/; and an import of a binding named `db` from any specifier other than 'void/db' or '@schema' re-exports.
rules.partial: Re-exports through another module escape. The tsconfig `paths` that define @schema are not read.

rules.name: use-void-drizzle-modules
rules.summary: Drizzle schema builders, query operators, types, validators and the db instance come from Void's modules, not from drizzle-orm packages.
rules.files: any file; any file except db/ seed and migration scripts
rules.detect: (1) Import specifier `drizzle-orm/sqlite-core`, `drizzle-orm/pg-core`, `drizzle-orm/mysql-core`, `drizzle-orm/d1`-family driver subpaths of those three cores, or a bare `drizzle-orm` import whose specifiers are table or column builders (sqliteTable, pgTable, mysqlTable, text, integer, real, blob, serial, varchar, ...). (2) ImportDeclaration from 'drizzle-orm' (not a subpath) with at least one specifier in: sql eq ne gt gte lt lte and or not desc asc like ilike notLike inArray notInArray isNull isNotNull between notBetween exists notExists count sum avg min max SQL SQLWrapper AnyColumn BatchItem. Type-only imports included. (3) Import of `drizzle` from 'drizzle-orm/d1', 'drizzle-orm/node-postgres', 'drizzle-orm/postgres-js', 'drizzle-orm/mysql2', or a call to the imported `drizzle(...)`. (4) Import specifier `drizzle-zod`, `drizzle-valibot` or `drizzle-arktype`.
rules.reports: the import specifier; the import; the import or call
rules.partial: A project with a drizzle-orm feature Void does not re-export (for example relations helpers imported from 'drizzle-orm') is untouched; only schema builders are targeted. Names Void does not re-export (`relations`, `getTableColumns`) are left alone. Multi-database setups use createDb from void/db, which this rule does not report.

rules.name: void-deploy-usage
rules.summary: 'void/deploy' is used only in Node tooling, and prepareCfBuildOutput results are disposed.
rules.files: files under routes/, pages/, middleware/, crons/, queues/, email/, durable-objects/ and browser code; Node.js tooling scripts
rules.detect: (1) Import (static or dynamic) of 'void/deploy' in a file under a convention directory. (2) A variable initialised from `await prepareCfBuildOutput(...)` with no `.dispose()` call anywhere in the same function; a dispose outside a `finally` block is reported at lower severity.
rules.partial: Disposal in another function escapes.

rules.name: no-server-module-in-browser
rules.summary: Page components and browser code do not import server-only Void modules.
rules.files: pages/** except *.server.* (components, _components, _features, _lib), plus files named *.island.* and *.tsx under pages/
rules.detect: Non-type ImportDeclaration or dynamic import of 'void/db', 'void/auth', 'void/storage', 'void/kv', 'void/ai', 'void/sandbox', 'void/queues', 'void/live', 'void/ws/server', 'void/email' in browser code (void/env is handled by no-server-env-in-browser). `import type` is allowed.
rules.partial: Only pages/ is treated as browser code; a helper outside pages/ imported by a component is not seen.

rules.name: no-server-secret-in-browser
rules.summary: Browser code reads no non-VITE_ env key and never mentions AUTH_TRUSTED_KEY.
rules.files: pages/** except *.server.* (browser code); pages/** except *.server.*, and src/** client files
rules.detect: (1) MemberExpression on the `env` binding imported from 'void/env' whose property name (identifier or string literal) does not start with `VITE_`. (2) Identifier, string literal, or member property named `AUTH_TRUSTED_KEY` in browser code.
rules.partial: Passing the key through another name escapes.

rules.name: no-sse-client-in-server
rules.summary: 'void/sse/client' is imported only in browser code, never in server files.
rules.files: routes/**, pages/**/*.server.*, middleware/**, queues/**, crons/**, email/**
rules.detect: Import of 'void/sse/client' in those files.

rules.name: no-value-import-from-server-file
rules.summary: Page components import from the companion .server file with `import type` only.
rules.detect: ImportDeclaration with a relative specifier ending in `.server` (or `.server.ts`) that is not `import type` and has no `type` specifier modifiers only.
rules.partial: A re-export of a server module through a barrel is not followed.

rules.name: basic-auth-credentials-lazy-env
rules.summary: basicAuth credentials come from void/env through callbacks, not string literals or direct env reads.
rules.files: middleware/** and any file calling basicAuth
rules.detect: In the options object of `basicAuth(...)` (from 'void'/'void/handler'): a username, password, realm or message property whose value is a Literal/TemplateLiteral, or a MemberExpression on `env` imported from 'void/env' (it must be an arrow or function returning it).
allowed: export default basicAuth({ username: () => env.GATE_USER, password: () => env.GATE_PASS });
export default basicAuth({ username: () => env.U, password: () => env.P, realm: () => 'Staging' });
reported: export default basicAuth({ username: env.GATE_USER, password: env.GATE_PASS });
rules.partial: A password read from a plain variable is not reported.

rules.name: define-handler-max-middleware
rules.summary: defineHandler takes at most five middleware before the handler.
rules.detect: CallExpression `defineHandler(...)` (imported from 'void'/'void/handler') with more than 6 arguments.
allowed: export const GET = defineHandler(m1, m2, m3, m4, m5, (c) => 1);
reported: export const GET = defineHandler(m1, m2, m3, m4, m5, m6, (c) => 1);
export const GET = defineHandler(a, b, c, d, e, f, g);

rules.name: hono-cache-placement
rules.summary: hono/cache is kept off pages and off routes that read the signed-in user.
rules.detect: (1) File imports `cache` from 'hono/cache' and also imports from 'void/auth' or calls getUser/getSession/requireAuth/getCookie or `c.req.header('cookie')`. (2) Import of 'hono/cache'.
allowed:
import { cache } from 'hono/cache';
export const GET = defineHandler(cache({ cacheName: 'p' }), () => []);
reported:
import { cache } from 'hono/cache';
export const GET = defineHandler(cache({}), (c) => c.req.header('cookie'));
rules.partial: A user read in an imported helper escapes.

rules.name: hono-declared-dependency
rules.summary: Hono packages imported directly are declared in the app's own package.json.
rules.detect: Import of those specifiers when the nearest package.json (read once per root by a lib helper) lists neither dependencies.hono nor devDependencies.hono (for `@hono/<x>` the package itself must be listed).
rules.partial: Reads package.json, which is not a source file but is a second input.

rules.name: hono-middleware-before-handler
rules.summary: Hono's per-route middleware (cache, cors, bearerAuth, ...) is passed as a leading argument of defineHandler, with the handler last.
rules.detect: Call of a function imported from 'hono/*' or '@hono/*' (a middleware factory) inside a defineHandler callback body, or as its last argument.
reported: export const GET = defineHandler((c) => { cache({ cacheName: 'p' }); return 1; });
export const GET = defineHandler((c) => 1, cache({ cacheName: 'p' }));
rules.partial: Middleware passed through variables escapes.

rules.name: http-exception-shape
rules.summary: HTTPException has a 4xx or 5xx status, or a 3xx status with a `res` that carries the redirect.
rules.detect: (1) NewExpression `new HTTPException(<numeric Literal>, ...)` whose first argument is outside 400-599 and is not a redirect (3xx with a `res` option is allowed). (2) `throw c.redirect(...)`; `new HTTPException(<3xx literal>, opts)` whose options object lacks a `res` property or has no second argument.
rules.reports: the first argument; the throw or the constructor
rules.partial: The 3xx-with-res redirect form is a separate rule (http-exception-redirect-res).

rules.name: redirect-after-mutation-303
rules.summary: A redirect after a mutation uses status 303, so the next request is a GET.
rules.detect: Inside `action` / `actions` exports or handlers exported as POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE: `c.redirect(url)` with no status or a status literal other than 303, and `new HTTPException(<3xx not 303>, ...)`.
rules.partial: Redirects issued from helpers escape; a redirect to the same GET page after a PRG is covered by 303 too.

rules.name: route-html-react-render
rules.summary: In React and Solid route handlers JSX is rendered to a string with the framework's server renderer before c.html().
rules.detect: CallExpression `c.html(<JSX/>)` whose argument is a JSXElement or JSXFragment directly.
rules.partial: Apps using Hono's own JSX runtime (jsxImportSource: hono/jsx) are valid and would be reported.

rules.name: with-validator-shape
rules.summary: defineHandler.withValidator is called with only body, query and params, and then called again with the handler.
rules.detect: (1) CallExpression `defineHandler.withValidator(args)` that is not the callee of another CallExpression, or that has two or more arguments. (2) ObjectExpression argument of `defineHandler.withValidator` with a property key other than body, query, params (computed keys and spreads are skipped).
allowed: export const POST = defineHandler.withValidator({ body })((c, { body }) => body);

const v = defineHandler.withValidator({ query });
export const GET = v((c, { query }) => query);
export const POST = defineHandler.withValidator({ body, query })((c, i) => i);
export const GET = defineHandler.withValidator({ params })((c, i) => i);
reported: export const POST = defineHandler.withValidator({ body }, (c, { body }) => body);
export const POST = defineHandler.withValidator({ json })((c, i) => i);
export const GET = defineHandler.withValidator({ headers })((c, i) => i);
rules.partial: In the second sample of allowed, the call is bound to a variable; the rule accepts a const initialised by withValidator that is later called.

rules.name: deferred-use-in-suspense
rules.summary: In React, a deferred prop is read with use() under a <Suspense> boundary, and rejection is left to an error boundary.
rules.detect: `use(x)` called in a file with no `<Suspense>` JSXElement anywhere; `use(x)` inside a TryStatement block.
allowed:
export default function P({ usage }) { return <Suspense fallback={null}><Usage usage={usage} /></Suspense>; }
function Usage({ usage }) { return use(usage).n; }
reported: export default function P({ usage }) { return use(usage).n; }
function U({ usage }) { try { return use(usage); } catch (e) { return null; } }
rules.partial: A Suspense in a parent layout in another file is not seen, so the first check can be wrong.

rules.name: dynamic-prerender-needs-paths
rules.summary: A dynamic page that opts into prerendering exports getPrerenderPaths() from the same .server file.
rules.detect: Module exporting `prerender = true` and no `getPrerenderPaths` export.
rules.partial: Under `output: 'static'` with no page flag the same requirement holds but needs the config.

rules.name: error-boundary-files
rules.summary: _error and _not-found components have no .server companion or layout export and type their props with ErrorPageProps.
rules.detect: (1) Report the Program of a file named `_error.server.*` or `_not-found.server.*` below pages/; in `_error.*` / `_not-found.*` component files report an export named `layout` (ExportNamedDeclaration with that name, or `export { layout }`). (2) Default-exported component whose first parameter has no type annotation, or whose annotation does not reference `ErrorPageProps` (imported from @void/react|vue|svelte|solid).
rules.reports: the Program or the `layout` export; the parameter
allowed:
// pages/_not-found.tsx export default function NotFound({ error }) { return

{error.message}

; }

// pages/_error.tsx
export default function E() { return null; }
reported:
// pages/_error.tsx
export default function E({ error }) { return null; }

// pages/_not-found.tsx
export default function N(props: { error: Error }) { return null; }
rules.partial: Boundary files are exempt from Void's `_` skip, which is why the path is checked explicitly. JavaScript pages carry no annotation and are skipped.

rules.name: get-prerender-paths-shape
rules.summary: getPrerenderPaths() exists only on dynamic pages, is annotated with PageParams, and returns every [param] of the path.
rules.detect: (1) Exported function or arrow `getPrerenderPaths` with no return type annotation, or an annotation that does not mention `PageParams`. (2) File path has no `[` segment and exports `getPrerenderPaths`. (3) When the function returns an ArrayExpression of ObjectExpressions: report an object missing a key named by a [param]/[...param] segment of the path, an unknown key, a value that is not string/number literal-ish, or a string literal containing `/` for a plain [param].
rules.reports: the function; the export; the object or value
allowed:
// pages/blog/[slug].server.ts
export async function getPrerenderPaths(): Promise<PageParams<'/blog/[slug]'>[]> { return []; }

// src/main.ssr.ts
export async function getPrerenderPaths(): Promise<string[]> { return []; }

// pages/blog/[slug].server.ts
export async function getPrerenderPaths() { return []; }

// pages/blog/[slug].server.ts
export const getPrerenderPaths = async () => [{ slug: 'hello' }];
reported:
// pages/blog/[slug].server.ts
export async function getPrerenderPaths() { return []; }

// pages/blog/[slug].server.ts
export const getPrerenderPaths = async (): Promise<string[]> => [];

// pages/about.server.ts
export async function getPrerenderPaths() { return []; }

// pages/blog/[slug].server.ts
export const getPrerenderPaths = async () => [{ id: 'hello' }];
rules.partial: src/main.ssr.* is excluded: it uses Promise<string[]>. Arrays built by map or database queries escape (the PageParams annotation makes tsc check them).

rules.name: layout-renders-children
rules.summary: A layout renders its children: {children} (React), props.children (Solid), {@render children()} (Svelte), <slot /> (Vue).
rules.detect: Layout component file in which no Identifier `children`, MemberExpression `props.children`, JSXElement `<slot>` or `@render children` appears.
allowed:
// pages/layout.tsx
export default function Layout({ children }) { return <main>{children}</main>; }

// pages/_layouts/landing.tsx export default function L(props) { return
{props.children}
; }
reported:
// pages/layout.tsx
export default function Layout() { return <main />; }

// pages/_layouts/landing.tsx
export default function L() { return null; }
rules.partial: Children forwarded through a wrapper in another file escape; Vue and Svelte templates are not linted.

rules.name: link-prefetch-options
rules.summary: prefetch uses valid strategies and cacheFor a valid shape.
rules.files: page components and config (Link prefetch, adapter plugin options); page components
rules.detect: (1) `prefetch` JSX attribute or `defaultStrategy` property whose literal value is not in {true,false,'hover','click','mount','visible'} or an array of those strings. (2) `cacheFor` attribute or property whose literal is not a number, a string, or an array of exactly two (number|string) elements.
rules.partial: The duration units Void accepts are not enumerated in the docs, so a string is never judged.

rules.name: link-prop-shape
rules.summary: A mutation Link has no prefetch or reloadDocument, and a GET Link's data holds scalars.
rules.files: page components and layouts (JSX; Vue/Svelte script and template where linted); page components
rules.detect: (1) JSXOpeningElement `<Link>` (imported from @void/<adapter>) with a `method` attribute whose literal value is not 'get' and a `prefetch` or `reloadDocument` attribute. (2) JSX `<Link>` (from @void/<adapter>) without `method` or with method='get' whose `data` attribute is an ObjectExpression containing a property whose value is an ObjectExpression or an array of ObjectExpressions.
rules.reports: the prefetch / reloadDocument attribute; the nested value
rules.partial: Vue and Svelte templates are not parsed by oxlint, so only JSX Link usage is seen; a method held in a variable escapes. data passed as a variable escapes.

rules.name: loader-return-serializable
rules.summary: A loader does not return functions or custom class instances.
rules.detect: Using the type of the loader's returned object: a property whose type is a function type or a class instance type other than Date, Map, Set, RegExp, URL, bigint, undefined, plain objects and arrays of those.
allowed:
// pages/a.server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler(() => ({ at: new Date() }));

// pages/a.server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler(() => ({ ids: new Set([1]) }));
reported:
// pages/a.server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler(() => ({ fmt: (n: number) => String(n) }));
rules.partial: Needs the checker; Response objects from c.json are the loaders/4 contradiction and are not judged here.

rules.name: loader-returns-object
rules.summary: A loader returns an object whose keys become props, not an array, string or other primitive.
rules.detect: In the function passed to `defineHandler` for `loader`, a ReturnStatement (or arrow expression body) that is an ArrayExpression, Literal or TemplateLiteral.
allowed:
// pages/a.server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler(() => ({ posts: [] }));

// pages/a.server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler(async () => ({ n: 1 }));
rules.partial: A returned variable or call result escapes.

rules.name: no-eager-prefetch
rules.summary: Prefer the 'hover' or 'click' prefetch strategies; 'mount' and 'visible' can load many pages in a long list.
rules.detect: `prefetch` attribute or `defaultStrategy` property with the literal 'mount' or 'visible' (alone or inside an array).
rules.partial: A preference, not a rule of Void: valid in short lists. Keep at warning or off by default.

rules.name: no-location-navigation
rules.summary: Internal navigation uses useRouter().visit(), not assignments to window.location or history.pushState.
rules.detect: AssignmentExpression to `window.location`, `location`, `location.href` or `window.location.href` whose right side is a string literal starting with a single `/`; calls `location.assign('/x')` / `location.replace('/x')` / `history.pushState(_, _, '/x')` with such a literal.
rules.partial: Intentional full reloads to internal paths (logout) are reported.

rules.name: no-param-by-name-in-page-server
rules.summary: Page loaders and actions read route params as `c.req.param() as PageParams<'/pattern'>`, not c.req.param('name').
rules.detect: CallExpression `c.req.param(<argument>)` with one argument.
allowed:
// pages/users/[id].server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler((c) => { const { id } = c.req.param() as PageParams<'/users/[id]'>; return { id }; });
reported:
// pages/users/[id].server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler((c) => ({ id: c.req.param('id') }));

// pages/users/[id].server.ts
export const action = defineHandler((c) => c.req.param('id'));

rules.name: no-solid-props-destructure
rules.summary: In Solid components, props are read inside JSX or memos, not destructured or copied into plain variables.
rules.detect: Component function (capitalised name returning JSX) whose first parameter is an ObjectPattern, or a top-level body `const x = props.y` outside a JSX expression, createMemo, createEffect.
allowed:
export default function B(props) { const n = createMemo(() => props.name); return

{n()}

; }
reported:
export default function A({ name }) { return

{name}

; }

export default function B(props) { const name = props.name; return

{name}

; }
rules.partial: Only for Solid; React components with destructured props are fine.

rules.name: no-status-in-defer
rules.summary: Status-deciding calls (c.status, redirects) finish before deferred streaming starts, not inside defer().
rules.detect: Inside a function passed to `defer(...)`: a `c.status(...)` call, a `c.redirect(...)` call, or `throw` of a redirect response/HTTPException with a 3xx status.
allowed:
// pages/a.server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler((c) => { if (!ok) c.status(404); return { slow: defer(async () => 1) }; });

// pages/a.server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler(() => ({ slow: defer(async () => { throw new HTTPException(500); }) }));
reported:
// pages/a.server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler((c) => ({ slow: defer(async () => { c.status(404); return 1; }) }));

// pages/a.server.ts
export const loader = defineHandler((c) => ({ slow: defer(async () => { throw c.redirect('/x'); }) }));
rules.partial: Throwing an HTTPException with a 4xx/5xx inside defer is allowed (loaders.md shows its message in the UI).

rules.name: page-isr-exports
rules.summary: The prerender and ssr exports are boolean literals, revalidate is a whole-number literal, and prerender is not combined with revalidate = 0.
rules.detect: (1) Export named `prerender` or `ssr` whose initialiser is not a boolean Literal; also `export { x as prerender }` and `export { prerender } from`. (2) `export const revalidate = <init>` where init is not a non-negative integer Literal; also `export { revalidate } from ...` and `export { x as revalidate }`. (3) A module exporting `prerender = true` and `revalidate = 0` (both literals).
rules.partial: A config-level revalidate of 0 is not visible.

rules.name: page-server-export-shape
rules.summary: A page's .server file exports loader/action built with defineHandler, not both action and actions, and no GET/POST handlers or default export.
rules.detect: (1) `export const loader|action = <init>` where init is not a CallExpression with callee `defineHandler` or `defineHandler.withValidator(...)`. Entries of an `actions` object literal are checked the same way. (2) A module with both a named export `action` and a named export `actions`. (3) Export named GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS or any ExportDefaultDeclaration.
rules.reports: the initialiser; the second export; the export
allowed:
// pages/a.server.ts
export const action = defineHandler.withValidator({ body })((c, { body }) => body);

// pages/a.server.ts
export const actions = { save: defineHandler(() => ({})) };
rules.partial: A handler imported or built by a factory is reported or skipped by whether it is a local call. Whether a sibling component file exists needs the filesystem and is not checked.

rules.name: server-exports-in-server-file
rules.summary: loader, action(s), head, ssr, prerender, getPrerenderPaths and revalidate are exported from a page's .server file, never from components or routes.
rules.files: pages/** component files (not *.server.*, not _-prefixed); any file except pages/**/*.server.*
rules.detect: (1) ExportNamedDeclaration (declaration, specifier or re-export) naming `loader`, `action`, `actions`, `head`, `ssr`, `prerender`, or `export const ... ` with those names. (2) `export const prerender` or `export function getPrerenderPaths` or `export const revalidate` (declaration, specifier) in a file that is not pages/**/*.server.*; src/main.ssr.* is exempt for prerender and getPrerenderPaths.
allowed:
// pages/about.tsx
export default function About() { return null; }
rules.partial: .vue/.svelte pages are linted only in their script block. A non-page module that happens to export a constant named revalidate (a helper) is reported; restrict via path if needed.

rules.name: set-preserves-shared
rules.summary: A loader or action that updates shared data spreads the existing value, so other keys survive.
rules.detect: `c.set('shared', <ObjectExpression>)` with no SpreadElement of `c.get('shared')`.
rules.partial: Building the object elsewhere escapes. Middleware setting shared first is allowed because this rule looks at .server files only.

rules.name: ssr-entry-prerender-paths
rules.summary: In custom SSR mode src/main.ssr.ts exports getPrerenderPaths() at the top level and it returns full path strings.
rules.detect: A `getPrerenderPaths` declared but not exported, or exported from a nested scope or via `export { x } from`; an ArrayExpression of ObjectExpressions returned from it, or a return type other than Promise<string[]>.
allowed:
// src/main.ssr.tsx
export async function getPrerenderPaths(): Promise<string[]> { return ['/a', '/b']; }
reported:
// src/main.ssr.tsx
export async function getPrerenderPaths() { return [{ slug: 'a' }]; }

rules.name: use-params-pattern-type-arg
rules.summary: useParams is called with the page pattern as the type argument.
rules.detect: CallExpression `useParams(...)` imported from @void/react|vue|svelte|solid with no typeArguments.
rules.partial: JavaScript files carry no type arguments and are skipped.

rules.name: view-transitions-option-name
rules.summary: The global option is viewTransitions: true (plural) on the adapter plugin; the per-link prop and router.visit option are viewTransition (singular).
rules.detect: In the options of voidReact|voidVue|voidSvelte|voidSolid: a property named `viewTransition` (singular) or `viewTransitions` with a non-boolean literal. On `<Link>` and router.visit/prefetch options: a property named `viewTransitions` (plural) or `view-transitions`.

rules.name: await-visit-resolve-on-data
rules.summary: Awaiting router.visit()/refresh() inside startTransition, useActionState, a <form action> or a useForm callback passes { resolveOn: 'data' }.
rules.detect: `await router.visit(...)` / `await router.refresh(...)` (router from useRouter) inside a function passed to startTransition, useActionState, useForm's onSuccess/onError, or used as a <form action> attribute, whose options argument lacks a property `resolveOn: 'data'`.
allowed: const form = useForm('/x', {}, { onSuccess: async () => { await router.visit('/y', { resolveOn: 'data' }); } });
reported: const form = useForm('/x', {}, { onSuccess: async () => { await router.visit('/y'); } });
rules.partial: Calls inside helpers escape.

rules.name: handle-action-result
rules.summary: The { ok: false, error } result of action() is handled, not ignored.
rules.detect: `await action(...)` (action from the adapter) as an ExpressionStatement with no binding, or a bound result whose `.pageData` is read with no `.ok` or `.error` access on the same binding.
allowed:
const r = await action('/x', body);
if (!r.ok) setError(r.error);

const r = await action('/x', body);
return r;
reported:
const r = await action('/x', body);
use(r.pageData);
rules.partial: Results passed to helpers escape.

rules.name: island-forms-use-island-hook
rules.summary: Forms in island components use useIslandForm and pass the action URL to the submit helper.
rules.detect: In a file named *.island.*: import of useForm or Form from an adapter package; a `.post|put|patch|delete()` call with zero arguments on a binding initialised from useIslandForm().
rules.partial: Island components in separate _Component files that are not named .island.* escape.

rules.name: narrow-action-error
rules.summary: A caught action error is narrowed with isVoidActionError() before its status or message is read.
rules.detect: In a catch clause or an `onError` parameter: a MemberExpression `.status` on the error binding with no `isVoidActionError(<binding>)` call in the same function.
allowed: try { await action('/x', b); } catch (e) { if (isVoidActionError(e)) show(e.status); }
try { await action('/x', b); } catch (e) { log(e); }
reported: try { await action('/x', b); } catch (e) { show(e.status); }
const f = useForm('/x', init, { onError: (e) => show(e.status) });
rules.partial: Other narrowing (instanceof, a type guard) escapes.

rules.name: no-file-metadata-as-key
rules.summary: Uploaded files are stored under server-generated keys; file.name and file.type from the browser are not used as the key.
rules.detect: `storage.put(<key>, ...)` (storage from 'void/storage', or a binding returned by createStorage) whose first argument contains a MemberExpression `.name` / `.type` of a File-like binding, `c.req.param(...)`, `c.req.query(...)`, `c.req.header(...)` or a property of the validated input, with no `crypto.randomUUID()` / nanoid / ulid call in the key expression.
rules.partial: Keys computed in helpers or from an identifier escape; a validated server slug may be a legitimate key and is reported.

rules.name: no-focus-in-form-callbacks
rules.summary: useForm's onSuccess and onError do not focus an element that appears after submission.
rules.detect: Calls to `.focus()` (on any expression) inside the `onSuccess` / `onError` callbacks of useForm options.
allowed: const f = useForm('/x', init, { onSuccess: () => setSent(true) });
reported: const f = useForm('/x', init, { onSuccess: () => { document.getElementById('done')?.focus(); } });
const f = useForm('/x', init, { onError: () => ref.current.focus() });
rules.partial: Focus through helpers escapes.

rules.name: preserve-scroll-placement
rules.summary: preserveScroll is the third argument of useForm in React, and an option of form.post() in Vue, Svelte and Solid.
rules.detect: In a file importing useForm from '@void/react': `form.post|put|patch|delete({ preserveScroll })`. In files importing from '@void/vue|svelte|solid': a third argument of useForm that has `preserveScroll`.
allowed: const f = useForm('/x', init, { preserveScroll: true });
reported:
// svelte
const f = useForm('/x', init, { preserveScroll: true });
rules.partial: The adapter is read from the import specifier.

rules.name: use-form-params-option
rules.summary: When the useForm URL has a [param] segment, the options carry `params`.
rules.detect: `useForm(<string Literal containing '[' and ']'>, ...)` whose third argument is missing or is an ObjectExpression with no `params` property.
allowed: const f = useForm('/posts/[id]', init, { params: { id } });
reported: const f = useForm('/posts/[id]', init, { preserveScroll: true });

rules.name: head-defaults-spread
rules.summary: Overriding headDefaults spreads the existing value so earlier middleware defaults survive.
rules.detect: `c.set('headDefaults', <ObjectExpression>)` whose object has no SpreadElement of `c.get('headDefaults')`, in a middleware file that is not the first (numeric prefix > 01) or that also calls `c.get('headDefaults')`.
rules.partial: A first middleware legitimately sets the whole value; the numeric prefix is the only signal for 'first'.

rules.name: no-browser-api-in-head
rules.summary: head() runs on the server only: it uses no window, document, localStorage or navigator.
rules.detect: Identifier reference to `window`, `document`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` or `navigator` (not shadowed) inside the function passed to defineHead.
allowed: export const head = defineHead((c) => ({ title: c.req.path }));
reported: export const head = defineHead(() => ({ title: document.title }));
export const head = defineHead(() => ({ title: localStorage.getItem('t') }));
rules.partial: Helpers called from head escape.

rules.name: title-template-value
rules.summary: Every non-empty titleTemplate contains %s, and an empty one is written '' rather than null, undefined or false.
rules.detect: (1) Property `titleTemplate` (in a head descriptor, in `c.set('headDefaults', {...})` or in the config's `head`) whose string Literal is non-empty and has no `%s`. (2) Property `titleTemplate` whose value is `null`, `undefined` or `false`.
allowed: export const head = defineHead(() => ({ titleTemplate: '%s | Blog' }));
export const head = defineHead(() => ({ titleTemplate: '%s | A' }));
reported: export const head = defineHead(() => ({ titleTemplate: false }));

rules.name: island-import-shape
rules.summary: Island imports use a valid strategy, an underscore-named component, and sit in a <name>.island.<ext> page.
rules.files: pages/**/*.island.* and pages/** files with `with { island: ... }` imports; pages/** (not .md, not *.server.*); pages/**
rules.detect: (1) ImportDeclaration with an `island` import attribute whose relative source's file name (or a parent directory below pages/) does not start with `_`. (2) File with an import carrying the `island` attribute whose file name does not contain `.island.`. (3) ImportAttribute with key `island` whose string value is not 'load', 'visible', 'idle' and does not match /^media:\(.+\)$/.
rules.reports: the import source; the import; the value
allowed:
// pages/blog.island.tsx
import C from './_C' with { island: 'load' };
reported:
// pages/blog.tsx
import C from './_C' with { island: 'load' };

// pages/home.tsx
import C from './_C' with { island: 'idle' };
rules.partial: Imports inside .md <script> blocks are not JavaScript files.

rules.name: island-no-router
rules.summary: Island pages and island components use plain <a href>, not Link or useRouter.
rules.detect: ImportDeclaration of `Link`, `useRouter`, `useNavigation` or `router` helpers from '@void/*' in a file named *.island.*.
rules.partial: Island components in separate _Component files and layouts escape.

rules.name: use-frontmatter-from-void-md
rules.summary: useFrontmatter() comes from '@void/md'; FrontmatterContext and setFrontmatter() are deprecated.
rules.detect: Import of `useFrontmatter` from a specifier other than '@void/md'; any use of `FrontmatterContext` or `setFrontmatter` imported from '@void/md'.
rules.partial: Whether a layout or island is the caller is not checked.

rules.name: void-markdown-plugin-setup
rules.summary: voidMarkdown() is registered, comes after the adapter plugin, and takes `themes` not the deprecated shiki option.
rules.detect: (1) In the `plugins` ArrayExpression, a CallExpression `voidMarkdown(...)` whose index is lower than the index of a `voidReact|voidVue|voidSvelte|voidSolid` call. (2) A file importing from '@void/md/plugin' whose `plugins` array has no `voidMarkdown(...)` call. (3) ObjectExpression argument of `voidMarkdown(...)` with a `shiki` property.
rules.reports: the voidMarkdown call; the import; the property
allowed:
import { voidMarkdown } from '@void/md/plugin';
export default { plugins: [voidReact(), voidMarkdown()] };
reported:
import { voidMarkdown } from '@void/md/plugin';
export default { plugins: [voidReact()] };

import { voidMarkdown } from '@void/md/plugin';
export default { plugins: [] };
rules.partial: Pages that import @void/md with no plugin configured need another file and are not seen.

rules.name: cloud-context-augmentation-module
rules.summary: Typed context variables are added by augmenting CloudContextVariables inside `declare module 'void'`.
rules.detect: An InterfaceDeclaration named `CloudContextVariables` that is not inside a `declare module 'void' { ... }` block, or a `declare module '<other>'` block that declares it.
allowed: declare module 'void' { interface CloudContextVariables { requestId: string } }
reported: declare module 'void/handler' { interface CloudContextVariables { requestId: string } }

rules.name: link-href-shape
rules.summary: Link and router destinations are absolute paths built with routeUrl(), not relative paths, template literals or concatenation.
rules.files: page components; page components and layouts
rules.detect: (1) `href` attribute of Link, or a string literal first argument of router.visit/prefetch, that starts with `./` or `../`. (2) `href` attribute of Link, or the first argument of `router.visit` / `prefetch` / `flush` / `c.redirect`, that is a TemplateLiteral with expressions or a BinaryExpression `+` whose left side is a string literal starting with `/`.
rules.partial: A URL stored in a variable first escapes; query strings added to a routeUrl result by template are reported too.

rules.name: no-any-cast-url
rules.summary: A trusted URL TypeScript cannot check is cast with `as Href`, not `as any` or `as string`.
rules.detect: TSAsExpression to `any` or `string` that is the argument of `c.redirect(...)`, the `href` of Link, or the first argument of router.visit.

rules.name: no-open-redirect
rules.summary: Request-derived redirect targets (?redirectTo=) are checked before c.redirect or c.rewrite; casting does not validate.
rules.detect: `c.redirect(x)` / `c.rewrite(x)` where x (after stripping `as Href` / `as RouteUrl` casts) is a direct call `c.req.query(...)`, `c.req.header(...)`, `c.req.param(...)` or a property of a validated body/query binding named like redirect/next/returnTo/url, with no `new URL(...)`, `.startsWith('/')` or origin comparison on it earlier in the function.
rules.partial: Validation done in another function escapes (reported, then false); keep this rule at warning level.

rules.name: no-stream-url-fragments
rules.summary: SSE and live stream clients receive only route URLs or http(s) URLs.
rules.detect: First argument of `connectEventStream(...)` / `connectLiveStream(...)` that is a string Literal starting with `#`, `?`, `mailto:`, `tel:` or `ws://`.

rules.name: route-types-from-void-routes
rules.summary: RouteMap and the route types are imported from 'void/routes', not 'void'.
rules.detect: Import of RouteMap, RouteUrl, Href, RoutePath, PagePath, PageParams, RouteOptions, RouteDestination, RouteUrlInput, RouteQuery, RoutePathMap, PagePathMap or RewriteDestination from a specifier other than 'void/routes'.

rules.name: route-url-params-shape
rules.summary: routeUrl() takes raw values, and a catch-all gets the whole remaining path as one value.
rules.detect: (1) A property value in the `params` object of `routeUrl(...)` that is a call to `encodeURIComponent` or `encodeURI`. (2) `routeUrl('<pattern with [...name]>', { params: { name: <ArrayExpression | .split(...) call | BinaryExpression '+' joining pieces> } })`.
rules.partial: Values built elsewhere escape.

rules.name: client-fetch-arguments
rules.summary: void/client fetch gets the route pattern with params/query options, an explicit method for non-GET calls, and a plain-object body.
rules.detect: (1) Call whose first argument is a string Literal containing `[` and `]` and whose options argument is missing or an ObjectExpression without `params`. (2) Call whose options ObjectExpression has a `body` property and no `method`, or whose type argument names a non-GET method but options lack `method`. (3) First argument that is a TemplateLiteral with expressions, a BinaryExpression `+`, or a string Literal containing `?`. (4) Option `body` that is a call to `JSON.stringify`; option `headers` setting Content-Type to application/json.
rules.reports: the call; the argument; the property

rules.name: client-fetch-no-json-call
rules.summary: The result of void/client fetch is parsed data; .json() is not called on it.
rules.detect: MemberCall `.json()` on `await fetch(...)`, on `fetch(...).then(r => r.json())`, or on a variable initialised from `await fetch(...)`.
allowed: const u = await fetch('/users', { query: { a: 1 } });
reported:
const r = await fetch('/users');
const d = await r.json();
rules.partial: Aliases through other functions escape.

rules.name: use-void-client-fetch
rules.summary: Your own API routes are called with fetch from 'void/client', not the global fetch.
rules.detect: Call to the global `fetch` (not imported) whose first argument is a string Literal or TemplateLiteral starting with `/`, with no file extension and not starting with `/api/auth/`.
rules.partial: Paths that are not Void routes (a CMS proxy, a rewrite target) are reported falsely.

rules.name: auth-no-static-schema-import
rules.summary: auth.ts does not statically import '@auth-schema' (or Void's own auth types); hooks import what they need with await import().
rules.detect: Static ImportDeclaration of '@auth-schema' in auth.ts; ImportDeclaration of AuthUser/AuthSession/AuthState or of getUser/getSession/getAuth/requireAuth from 'void/auth'.
allowed:
// auth.ts
hooks: { after: async () => { const { userTable } = await import('@auth-schema'); } }
rules.partial: Modules imported by auth.ts are not checked.

rules.name: no-x-forwarded-for-in-auth
rules.summary: auth.ts does not read the client IP from x-forwarded-for; rate-limit bypass uses a secret header check.
rules.detect: A string Literal `'x-forwarded-for'` (case-insensitive) as an argument of `.get(...)` or `.header(...)`, or as a property key, in auth.ts.

rules.name: prefer-require-auth-redirect
rules.summary: A sign-in guard uses requireAuth(c, { throwRedirect: '/login' }) instead of hand-throwing the redirect HTTPException.
rules.detect: IfStatement whose test is `!getUser()` / `!user` after a getUser() call and whose body throws `new HTTPException(302|303, { res: c.redirect('/login'...) })`.
reported: if (!getUser()) throw new HTTPException(303, { res: c.redirect('/login', 303) });

const u = getUser();
if (!u) throw new HTTPException(302, { res: c.redirect('/login') });
rules.partial: Other guard shapes escape.

rules.name: require-auth-throw-redirect-literal
rules.summary: requireAuth's throwRedirect is a trusted in-app path, never a value taken from the request.
rules.detect: `requireAuth(c, { throwRedirect })` whose throwRedirect value is not a string Literal starting with a single `/`: a call of c.req.query/header/param, or a member of validated input, is reported.
rules.partial: Validation done in another function escapes; a constant held in a variable is not followed.

rules.name: env-schema-safe-keys
rules.summary: env.ts and VITE_ variables hold no secrets: no secret under a VITE_ name, no credential in .default(...), no PUBLIC_ prefix.
rules.files: env.ts, and any file reading import.meta.env; env.ts
rules.detect: (1) In env.ts a property key of the defineEnv object that starts with `VITE_` and contains SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, PRIVATE, KEY (excluding PUBLISHABLE and ORIGIN); anywhere, `import.meta.env.VITE_<NAME>` where NAME has those words (and API_KEY). (2) `.default(<non-empty string Literal>)` on a defineEnv property whose key contains KEY, SECRET, TOKEN or PASSWORD (excluding PUBLISHABLE). (3) Key of the defineEnv object starting with `PUBLIC_`.
rules.reports: the key or the member access; the default call; the key
allowed:
// env.ts
export default defineEnv({ VITE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: z.string() });

// env.ts
export default defineEnv({ API_KEY: z.string(), REGION: z.string().default('eu') });

// env.ts
export default defineEnv({ MODE: z.string().default('dev') });

// env.ts
export default defineEnv({ VITE_SITE_URL: z.string() });
reported:
// env.ts
export default defineEnv({ VITE_STRIPE_SECRET: z.string() });

// env.ts
export default defineEnv({ API_KEY: z.string().default('abc123') });

// env.ts
export default defineEnv({ SESSION_SECRET: z.string().default('x') });

// env.ts
export default defineEnv({ PUBLIC_SITE_URL: z.string() });
rules.partial: A public key whose name contains KEY is reported unless it also contains PUBLISHABLE or ORIGIN; names are the only signal. Credentials under non-obvious names escape.

rules.name: no-alias-import-in-config-files
rules.summary: void.config.ts and env.ts import only relative paths or packages, never tsconfig path aliases or Vite-transformed imports.
rules.detect: Import specifier starting with `@/`, `~/`, `#`, or ending with a Vite query (`?raw`, `?url`, `?inline`).
rules.partial: Aliases without a recognisable prefix escape (the tsconfig is not read).

rules.name: db-batch-not-empty
rules.summary: db.batch() on D1 receives at least one query.
rules.detect: `db.batch([])` with an empty ArrayExpression.
rules.partial: A runtime-built array that may be empty escapes.

rules.name: db-bookmark-returned
rules.summary: A createDb client built with an incoming bookmark returns getBookmark(client) in the response.
rules.detect: `createDb(..., { session: { bookmark } })` whose enclosing file has no `getBookmark(<that client>)` call.
allowed:
const client = createDb(env.DB2, { session: { bookmark: b } });
c.header('x-bookmark', getBookmark(client));
reported:
const client = createDb(env.DB2, { session: { bookmark: b } });
return c.json(await client.query.users.findMany());
rules.partial: The client passed into other modules escapes.

rules.name: db-session-in-request-scope
rules.summary: setSession(), the no-argument getBookmark() and a createDb() with a session option run inside the request, never at module scope.
rules.detect: CallExpression `setSession(...)`, `getBookmark()` (no arguments) or `createDb(..., { session })` that is not inside any function (module top level).
allowed: export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { setSession('first-primary'); await next(); });
export const GET = defineHandler((c) => { const d = createDb(c.env.DB, { session: 'first-primary' }); return 1; });
rules.partial: Calls inside helper functions that run outside a request escape.

rules.name: set-session-usage
rules.summary: setSession() is called in middleware, before db use and before next(), with a valid argument.
rules.files: any file importing setSession from 'void/db'; middleware/**; any file calling setSession
rules.detect: (1) CallExpression `setSession(...)` in a file not under middleware/. (2) A member access on `db` earlier in source order than the `setSession(...)` call in the same function; `setSession` after `await next()`; `getBookmark()` before `await next()`. (3) `setSession(<arg>)` where arg is a string Literal other than the two names, or a call to `getBookmark()` / a header read not wrapped in `{ bookmark: ... }`.
rules.reports: the call; the offending call; the argument
allowed: export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { setSession('first-primary'); await next(); c.header('x-bookmark', getBookmark()); });
reported: export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { await db.query.users.findMany(); setSession('first-primary'); await next(); });
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { await next(); setSession('first-primary'); });
rules.partial: Use of db in other middleware escapes. The type check would also catch this; the lint needs no checker.

rules.name: ai-gateway-options-third-arg
rules.summary: AI Gateway options (skipCache, cacheTtl) are the third argument of ai.run.
rules.detect: `ai.run(model, inputs)` whose `inputs` ObjectExpression has a `gateway` property.
allowed: await ai.run(m, inputs, { gateway: { skipCache: true } });
reported: await ai.run(m, { prompt: 'a', gateway: { skipCache: true } });

rules.name: ai-stream-returned
rules.summary: ai.stream(...) is returned from the handler, not awaited into c.json.
rules.detect: `ai.stream(...)` whose result is awaited and passed to `c.json(...)` / `JSON.stringify(...)`, or assigned to a variable that is never returned.
allowed: export const POST = defineHandler((c) => ai.stream(m, i));
reported:
const s = ai.stream(model, input);
return c.text('ok');

rules.name: background-usage-limit-handled
rules.summary: ai.* calls in queues and cron jobs handle the rejected UsageLimit themselves.
rules.detect: `ai.run|stream|image|toMarkdown(...)` with no enclosing TryStatement and no `.catch` in the same function.
allowed:
// crons/a.ts
try { await ai.run(m, i); } catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof UsageLimit)) throw e; }
reported:
// crons/a.ts
const r = await ai.run(m, i);
rules.partial: Handling in callers escapes.

rules.name: fetch-stream-caught
rules.summary: fetchStream() calls in the UI catch UsageLimit and StreamError.
rules.detect: `fetchStream(...)` (from 'void/client') not inside a TryStatement block, with no `.catch(...)` chained.
allowed: try { for await (const c of fetchStream('/chat', {})) add(c); } catch (e) { retry(); }
reported: for await (const c of fetchStream('/chat', {})) add(c);
rules.partial: Callers further up the stack that catch escape as false reports.

rules.name: inbound-email-usage
rules.summary: Inbound email handlers call parseEmail once, use replyEmail only inside email/, and pass bare addresses to forward/reply.
rules.detect: (1) `replyEmail(...)` call in a file not under email/. (2) `.forward(<string Literal with '<' and '>'>)` and a `to`/`from` string Literal of `message.reply({...})` with a display name. (3) Two or more `parseEmail(<same Identifier>)` calls in one function.
rules.reports: the call; the literal; the second call
allowed:
// routes/a.ts
await sendEmail({ to, subject, text, threading });

rules.name: kv-put-arguments
rules.summary: kv.put gets values directly (no JSON.stringify) and ttl/expiration in seconds.
rules.detect: (1) `kv.put(key, JSON.stringify(...))`, including on a `kv.map(...)` client. (2) In the options of `kv.put`: `expiration` that contains `Date.now()` with no `/ 1000` or `Math.floor` division; `ttl` containing `Date.now()` or a `* 1000` factor.
rules.partial: Heuristic; unit mistakes in other shapes escape.

rules.name: logging-usage
rules.summary: Only logger.error/warn/info/child are used, and errors are logged as the Error object.
rules.files: any file importing logger from 'void/log'; any file
rules.detect: (1) MemberExpression on `logger` whose property is not error, warn, info or child. (2) `console.error(...)` / `logger.error(...)` whose non-literal arguments are all `<catchParam>.message` member expressions of a catch parameter and none is the catch parameter itself.
allowed: try { x(); } catch (error) { console.error('Save failed:', error); }
reported: try { x(); } catch (error) { console.error('Save failed:', error.message); }

rules.name: no-computed-env-binding
rules.summary: Bindings are read by static names (c.env.DB, destructuring); runtime-chosen keys are declared with inference.bindings.
rules.detect: Computed MemberExpression `c.env[expr]` / `env[expr]` where expr is not a string Literal, and a spread of `c.env`.
rules.partial: Apps that declared inference.bindings for runtime keys are reported; keep at warning level.

rules.name: no-send-in-dev
rules.summary: The deprecated sendInDev option is removed.
rules.detect: Property named `sendInDev` in any object literal.
reported: export default defineConfig({ email: { from: 'a@x.dev', sendInDev: true } });
await sendEmail({ to, subject, text, sendInDev: true });

rules.name: queue-no-swallowed-error
rules.summary: A queue consumer does not swallow errors: a catch that neither retries nor rethrows acknowledges the message.
rules.detect: A CatchClause inside the default-exported defineQueue handler with no ThrowStatement and no `.retry()` / `.retryAll()` call.
allowed:
// queues/a.ts
export default defineQueue<M>(async (b) => { try { await go(); } catch (e) { msg.retry(); } });

// queues/a.ts
export default defineQueue<M>(async (b) => { await go(); });
reported:
// queues/a.ts
export default defineQueue<M>(async (b) => { try { await go(); } catch (e) { log(e); } });

// queues/a.ts
export default defineQueue<M>(async (b) => { try { await go(); } catch {} });
rules.partial: A helper that does the retry escapes.

rules.name: sandbox-call-shape
rules.summary: sandbox.run/exec take an argument array and sandbox.files.* with relative paths pass cwd.
rules.detect: (1) `.run(<first>)` / `.exec(<first>)` on a binding initialised from `getSandbox(...)` where the first argument is a string Literal or TemplateLiteral. (2) `<sandbox>.files.<op>(<string Literal not starting with '/'>, ...)` with no `cwd` option.

rules.name: sandbox-get-options
rules.summary: getSandbox() gets an id of 1-63 characters and an inactivityTimeoutMs of at most six hours.
rules.detect: (1) `getSandbox(<string Literal>)` with an empty string or more than 63 characters. (2) `inactivityTimeoutMs` numeric Literal (or literal arithmetic) above 21600000.
rules.partial: Dynamic ids escape.

rules.name: sandbox-output-decoded
rules.summary: run() returns stdout and stderr as ArrayBuffer; they are decoded before being used as strings.
rules.detect: A `stdout` / `stderr` property of the run() result used in a template literal, in `+` string concatenation, in JSON.stringify or as a string-method receiver, when its type is ArrayBuffer.
allowed:
const r = await sb.run(['ls']);
const out = new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout);

const r = await sb.run(['ls']);
return new Response(r.stdout);
reported:
const r = await sb.run(['ls']);
const s = `out: ${r.stdout}`;

const r = await sb.run(['ls']);
const t = r.stderr + '!';
rules.partial: Needs types.

rules.name: send-email-idempotency-in-retries
rules.summary: sendEmail calls in queue consumers and cron jobs pass an idempotencyKey.
rules.detect: `sendEmail({...})` ObjectExpression with no `idempotencyKey` property.
allowed:
// queues/a.ts
await sendEmail({ to, subject, text, idempotencyKey: msg.id });

// routes/a.ts
await sendEmail({ to, subject, text });
reported:
// queues/a.ts
await sendEmail({ to, subject, text });

// crons/a.ts
await sendEmail({ to, subject, html });

rules.name: send-email-options
rules.summary: sendEmail options are complete and within the documented limits: to, subject, text or html, headers, idempotencyKey, recipient count, addresses, attachments.
rules.detect: (1) `sendEmail({...})` ObjectExpression (no spread) without a `to`, without a `subject`, or with neither `text` nor `html`. (2) Keys of the `headers` object of sendEmail (case-insensitive): From, Date, To, Subject, Message-ID, MIME-Version, Content-Type, In-Reply-To, References.
