(3) `idempotencyKey` string Literal empty, over 128 characters, or containing whitespace/non-ASCII; `to`/`cc`/`bcc` array literals whose combined element count exceeds 50; address string Literals with non-ASCII characters; attachment `contentType` Literals not matching /^[\w.+-]+\/[\w.+-]+/. (4) Attachment object with `contentId` and no `disposition: 'inline'`, or `disposition: 'inline'` with no `contentId`.
rules.reports: the object; the key; the literal; the attachment
allowed: await sendEmail({ to: a, subject: 's', text: 't' });

await sendEmail({ to: a, subject: 's', html: '

t

' });
await sendEmail({ to, subject, text, headers: { 'X-Campaign': 'a' } });
await sendEmail({ to, subject, text, threading: { inReplyTo: id } });
await sendEmail({ to: ['a@x.dev'], subject, text, idempotencyKey: 'order-42' });
reported: await sendEmail({ to, subject, text, headers: { From: 'a@b.c' } });
await sendEmail({ to, subject, text, headers: { 'In-Reply-To': id } });
await sendEmail({ to, subject, text, idempotencyKey: 'has space' });
rules.partial: The docs name From and Date; the rest of the list is the standard envelope headers. Only literals are judged.

rules.name: send-email-result-checked
rules.summary: sendEmail returns a result instead of throwing; the result is inspected, covering both result.error and result.deliveries.
rules.detect: `sendEmail(...)` as an ExpressionStatement (result discarded, with or without await); a result variable tested with `.ok` that never references both `.error` and `.deliveries`; a try/catch around sendEmail with no result check.
allowed:
const r = await sendEmail(m);
if (!r.ok) log(r.error, r.deliveries);
rules.partial: Results passed to helpers escape.

rules.name: served-upload-nosniff
rules.summary: A response that serves stored files sets X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
rules.detect: `new Response(<x>.body, ...)` or `c.body(<x>.body)` where <x> comes from `storage.get(...)`, and no `X-Content-Type-Options` header is set anywhere in the file.
allowed:
const o = await storage.get(key);
return new Response(o.body, { headers: { 'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff' } });
reported:
const o = await storage.get(key);
return new Response(o.body);

const o = await storage.get(key);
return c.body(o.body);
rules.partial: Headers set by middleware escape.

rules.name: usage-limit-handling
rules.summary: UsageLimit is imported from 'void/limits' and detected with instanceof; a handler returns error.response() and rethrows other errors.
rules.detect: Import of `UsageLimit` from a specifier other than 'void/limits' (or the client re-export); catch-clause tests `e.name === 'UsageLimit'` or on `e.message`; a catch with an `instanceof UsageLimit` check whose else path has no throw.
allowed: try { await ai.run(m, i); } catch (e) { if (e instanceof UsageLimit) return e.response({ message: 'busy' }); throw e; }
reported: try { await ai.run(m, i); } catch (e) { if (e.name === 'UsageLimit') return null; }
rules.partial: A catch that rethrows through a helper escapes.

rules.name: durable-state-migrations
rules.summary: Durable state migration versions start at 1, are contiguous, and `version` matches the last one.
rules.detect: In `defineDurableState({ version, migrations })`: literal migration versions not 1..n in order, or a literal `version` not equal to n.
allowed: defineDurableState({ version: 2, migrations: [{ version: 1, up }, { version: 2, up }] });
reported: defineDurableState({ version: 3, migrations: [{ version: 1, up }, { version: 3, up }] });
rules.partial: Non-literal versions escape.

rules.name: durable-state-reserved-methods
rules.summary: A durable state's methods are not named fetch, alarm or constructor; fetch and alarm are top-level hooks.
rules.detect: Property keys `fetch`, `alarm` or `constructor` inside the `methods` ObjectExpression of defineDurableState.

rules.name: event-source-no-headers
rules.summary: connectEventStream wraps EventSource: no headers, body or method options.
rules.detect: `connectEventStream(url, { headers | body | method })` options with any of those properties.

rules.name: event-stream-text-data
rules.summary: SSE data is a string or JSON-serialisable value, never binary.
rules.detect: `stream.send({ data })` where the type of `data` is ArrayBuffer, a TypedArray, Blob or a function.
rules.partial: Needs types.

rules.name: event-stream-usage
rules.summary: eventStream(...) is returned from the handler and a long-lived start callback awaits stream.closed.
rules.detect: (1) `eventStream(...)` whose result is discarded, assigned to a variable that is not returned, or passed to `c.json`. (2) In the start callback of `eventStream`: a `setInterval` / `setTimeout` call or an event-listener registration with no `await` of `stream.closed` or other promise in the callback.
allowed: export const GET = defineHandler((c) => eventStream(c, async (stream) => { await stream.closed; }));
eventStream(c, async (stream) => { const t = setInterval(() => stream.send({ data: 1 }), 1000); await stream.closed; clearInterval(t); });
reported: export const GET = defineHandler((c) => { eventStream(c, start); return c.text('ok'); });
export const GET = defineHandler((c) => c.json(eventStream(c, start)));
rules.partial: Other awaits that keep the stream open escape as false reports.

rules.name: format-sse-text
rules.summary: A payload that is already serialised is framed with formatSseText(), not hand-written SSE lines.
rules.detect: String Literal or TemplateLiteral that starts with `data:` or `event:` and contains `\n\n`, returned or passed to a Response.
rules.partial: Heuristic on the literal's shape.

rules.name: live-connect-client-import
rules.summary: Browsers subscribe with connectLiveStream from 'void/live/client'.
rules.detect: Import of `connectLiveStream` from a specifier other than 'void/live/client'.

rules.name: live-distinct-subscription-ids
rules.summary: Every subscription on one connection has its own id; reusing an id replaces the earlier subscription.
rules.detect: Two `<stream>.subscribe({ id: '<same string literal>', ... })` calls on the same receiver in one function or module.
allowed:
stream.subscribe({ id: 'a', topic: 'x' });
stream.subscribe({ id: 'b', topic: 'y' });
reported:
stream.subscribe({ id: 'a', topic: 'x' });
stream.subscribe({ id: 'a', topic: 'y' });

rules.name: live-route-pair
rules.summary: A live stream route exports GET calling live.connect(c) and POST calling live.control(c), and passes the same owner key to both.
rules.detect: `<stream>.connect(c...)` outside an exported GET, or `<stream>.control(c...)` outside an exported POST; a file calling one without the other; `owner` option expressions of connect and control that are not textually identical.
allowed:
export const GET = defineHandler((c) => live.connect(c));
export const POST = defineHandler((c) => live.control(c));

export const GET = defineHandler((c) => live.connect(c, { owner }));
export const POST = defineHandler((c) => live.control(c, { owner }));
reported:
export const GET = defineHandler((c) => live.connect(c, { owner: a }));
export const POST = defineHandler((c) => live.control(c, { owner: b }));

rules.name: live-stream-options
rules.summary: defineLiveStream has an id and limits.maxSubscriptionsPerTopic of at most 256.
rules.files: any file importing defineLiveStream from 'void/live'; any file importing defineLiveStream
rules.detect: (1) `defineLiveStream(...)` with no argument, a non-object argument, or an ObjectExpression with no `id` property. (2) `limits.maxSubscriptionsPerTopic` numeric Literal above 256.
allowed: export const feed = defineLiveStream({ id: 'feed', onSubscribe });
rules.partial: Required-ness of `id` is inferred from every example, not stated.

rules.name: no-boolean-return-in-guard-hooks
rules.summary: onSubscribe and onBeforeConnect reject by returning a Response and accept by returning nothing; they do not return booleans.
rules.files: any file defining a live stream, room or WebSocket
rules.detect: In the `onSubscribe` / `onBeforeConnect` function of a defineLiveStream / defineRoom / defineWebSocket options: a ReturnStatement (or arrow body) that is a boolean, null or string Literal.
allowed: defineRoom({ messages, onBeforeConnect: (ctx) => { if (!ctx.user) return new Response('no', { status: 401 }); } });
reported: defineLiveStream({ id: 'a', onSubscribe: ({ topic }) => { return false; } });

rules.name: no-get-room-in-own-hooks
rules.summary: A room's own hooks use ctx.room, not getRoom().
rules.detect: `getRoom(...)` call inside a hook function of the same file's default-exported defineRoom.

rules.name: room-action-definitions
rules.summary: Room actions annotate their parameters and do not read ctx.request or ctx.user.
rules.detect: (1) In the `actions` object of defineRoom: a function whose second or later parameter has no type annotation (TypeScript files only). (2) MemberExpression `ctx.request` or `ctx.user` (first parameter of the function) inside functions of the `actions` object.

rules.name: room-action-structured-clone-args
rules.summary: Arguments to room actions are structured-clone data: no functions or class instances.
rules.detect: Call `<x>.actions.<name>(...)` where x comes from `getRoom(...)`, with an argument that is an ArrowFunctionExpression, FunctionExpression or `new X(...)`.

rules.name: room-definition-options
rules.summary: defineRoom/defineWebSocket/defineDurableState options are valid: messages schemas, a synchronous key, a static name.
rules.detect: (1) `defineRoom(...)` / `defineWebSocket(...)` ObjectExpression without `messages`, or whose `messages` ObjectExpression lacks `client` or `server`. (2) `key` option that is an async function, a function containing `await`, a function returning a non-string Literal, or one returning `Math.random()` / `Date.now()` / `crypto.randomUUID()`. (3) `name` option whose value is not a string Literal or an Identifier bound to a `const` string Literal in the same file; for defineDurableState a literal not matching /^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z][a-z0-9]*)*$/.
rules.reports: the call; the key function; the value
allowed: export default defineRoom({ messages: { client: z.object({}), server: z.object({}) } });
reported: export default defineWebSocket({ messages: { client: z.object({}) } });
rules.partial: A `messages` passed by identifier is not looked into.

rules.name: ws-cookie-origin-check
rules.summary: Reading cookies from ctx.request in onBeforeConnect checks the Origin header.
rules.detect: In `onBeforeConnect`: `ctx.request.headers.get('cookie')` or a cookie helper on `ctx.request` with no reference to an `origin` header (string 'origin') in the same hook.
allowed: onBeforeConnect: (ctx) => { if (ctx.request.headers.get('origin') !== site) return new Response('no', { status: 403 }); const c = ctx.request.headers.get('cookie'); }
rules.partial: Origin checks in helpers escape.

rules.name: ws-hook-usage
rules.summary: onClose does not close the socket again, and onMessage/onClose do not read ctx.request.
rules.detect: (1) `ctx.connection.close()` / `ctx.socket.close()` inside the `onClose` function. (2) MemberExpression `ctx.request.headers`, `.url` or `.cookies` inside `onMessage` or `onClose`.

rules.name: ws-send-json-only
rules.summary: WebSocket messages are JSON events; no raw strings or binary through broadcast or send.
rules.detect: `ctx.room.broadcast(...)`, `ctx.connection.send(...)` or `ctx.socket.send(...)` whose argument is a string Literal, TemplateLiteral or `new ArrayBuffer/Uint8Array(...)`.

rules.name: config-always-https-cloudflare-only
rules.summary: routing.alwaysUseHttps is used only with the Cloudflare target.
rules.detect: `routing.alwaysUseHttps: true` in a config whose `target` literal is 'node', 'bun' or 'deno'.
allowed: export default defineConfig({ routing: { alwaysUseHttps: true } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ target: 'node', routing: { alwaysUseHttps: true } });
export default defineConfig({ target: 'deno', routing: { alwaysUseHttps: true } });

rules.name: config-cloudflare-placement
rules.summary: Cloudflare settings sit under `cloudflare` (binding arrays, routes, name, no environments), `deploy` is top-level, and deploy.cloudflare.mode is valid.
rules.detect: (1) In the defineConfig object or its `worker` object: a property named d1_databases, kv_namespaces, r2_buckets, services, durable_objects, queues, routes, route, name, account_id, migrations, vectorize, ai, hyperdrive. `vars` is excluded (worker.vars is documented). (2) `cloudflare` object with a property `env` or `environments`. (3) `cloudflare` object with a property `route` (singular). (4) A `deploy` property inside the `cloudflare` object; `deploy.cloudflare.mode` string Literal other than 'staged' or 'atomic'.
rules.reports: the property; the property or the literal
allowed: export default defineConfig({ worker: { vars: { A: '1' } } });
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { routes: [{ pattern: 'a.dev', custom_domain: true }] } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { env: { staging: {} } } });
rules.partial: config/36 lists `vars` under cloudflare while config/31 and cloudflare/7 put vars under worker, so vars is left alone.

rules.name: config-database-options
rules.summary: The database option, read replication and D1 migrations_dir are valid.
rules.detect: (1) `database` property whose literal is a string other than 'pg' or 'mysql', or an object whose `dialect` is not 'sqlite'|'pg'|'mysql', `casing` not 'snake_case'|'camelCase', `readReplication` not a boolean. (2) `database.readReplication` that is not a boolean Literal, or that is present together with `dialect: 'pg'` / `'mysql'` or `database: 'pg'` shape. (3) ObjectExpression inside `cloudflare.d1_databases` (array literal) without a `migrations_dir` property.
rules.reports: the value; the property; the binding object
allowed: export default defineConfig({ database: { dialect: 'mysql', casing: 'snake_case' } });
export default defineConfig({ database: { readReplication: true } });
export default defineConfig({ database: { dialect: 'sqlite', readReplication: true } });
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { d1_databases: [{ binding: 'DB', database_name: 'x', migrations_dir: 'db/migrations' }] } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ database: { dialect: 'pg', casing: 'kebab' } });
export default defineConfig({ database: { dialect: 'pg', readReplication: true } });
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { d1_databases: [{ binding: 'DB', database_name: 'x' }] } });
rules.partial: Bindings built from variables or kept only in void.lock.json escape.

rules.name: config-enum-options
rules.summary: auth.providers, target, storage.locationHint and sandbox.instanceType/platformImage hold documented values.
rules.detect: (1) String Literal in the `auth.providers` array not in: email apple atlassian cognito discord dropbox facebook figma github gitlab google huggingface kakao kick line linear linkedin microsoft naver notion paybin paypal polar railway reddit roblox salesforce slack spotify tiktok twitch twitter vercel vk zoom. (2) `target` string Literal not in those four. (3) `storage.locationHint` string Literal not in that set. (4) `sandbox.instanceType` literal not in {lite, basic, standard-1, standard-2, standard-3, standard-4}; `sandbox.platformImage` literal not matching /^registry\.cloudflare\.com\/.+@sha256:[0-9a-f]+$/.
rules.partial: RF config/21 only requires '@sha256:'; the stricter registry host comes from services/sandboxes/18.

rules.name: config-file-define-config
rules.summary: void.config.ts default-exports defineConfig(...) imported from 'void/config'.
rules.detect: No `export default`, or the default export is not a call to `defineConfig` imported from 'void/config' (importing it from 'vite' or 'void' is reported at the import). An identifier default export is followed to a same-file const.
rules.reports: the default export or the import
rules.partial: 'Beside package.json' (config/1) is not checked.

rules.name: config-worker-values
rules.summary: worker.vars values are strings and worker.limits.cpu_ms is 1-300000.
rules.detect: (1) Property value in `worker.vars` that is not a string Literal or TemplateLiteral. (2) `cpu_ms` numeric Literal below 1, above 300000 or not an integer.
allowed: export default defineConfig({ worker: { vars: { REGION: 'eu' } } });
export default defineConfig({ worker: { vars: { A: `x` } } });
export default defineConfig({ worker: { limits: { cpu_ms: 50 } } });
export default defineConfig({ worker: { limits: { cpu_ms: 300000 } } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ worker: { vars: { DEBUG: true } } });
export default defineConfig({ worker: { vars: { N: 3 } } });
export default defineConfig({ worker: { limits: { cpu_ms: 0 } } });
export default defineConfig({ worker: { limits: { cpu_ms: 400000 } } });

rules.name: email-from-format
rules.summary: email.from is one address, optionally with a display name (Name <addr>).
rules.detect: `email.from` string Literal that is not `addr@host` or `Name <addr@host>` (regexp), or contains more than one address.
reported: export default defineConfig({ email: { from: 'a@x.dev, b@x.dev' } });
rules.partial: Zone ownership is not checkable.

rules.name: inference-config-values
rules.summary: inference.appType is 'void', 'framework', 'spa' or 'static'; outputDir only with spa/static; bindings are true/false/string (email boolean); scanDirs are relative.
rules.detect: In `inference`: `appType` literal outside the four; `outputDir` present with an `appType` literal other than 'spa'/'static'; `bindings` keys outside db, kv, storage, ai, email or values that are not boolean/string (email: boolean only); `scanDirs` entries starting with `/` or a drive letter.
allowed: export default defineConfig({ inference: { appType: 'spa', outputDir: 'dist', bindings: { db: 'MY_DB', email: true } } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ inference: { appType: 'void', outputDir: 'dist', bindings: { email: 'E' } } });
rules.partial: One rule per option would be a dozen tiny rules; merged because every check is a literal enum on the same object.

rules.name: no-duplicate-framework-plugin
rules.summary: The framework's own Vite plugin (react(), vue(), svelte(), solid()) is not added next to the Void adapter; its options go through the adapter.
rules.detect: A file that calls `voidReact|voidVue|voidSvelte|voidSolid` in `plugins` and also imports the default export of @vitejs/plugin-react, @vitejs/plugin-react-swc, @vitejs/plugin-vue, @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte or vite-plugin-solid and calls it in `plugins`.
allowed: export default { plugins: [voidPlugin(), voidReact({ react: { babel: {} } })] };
reported:
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
export default { plugins: [voidPlugin(), voidReact(), react()] };

import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue';
export default { plugins: [voidPlugin(), voidVue(), vue()] };
rules.partial: Plugins added through helper functions escape.

rules.name: no-empty-assets-dir
rules.summary: build.assetsDir is not the empty string.
rules.detect: `build.assetsDir: ''` in the Vite config object.

rules.name: pages-adapter-plugin-present
rules.summary: A Pages-mode Vite config has both voidPlugin() and an adapter plugin (voidReact, voidVue, voidSvelte, voidSolid).
rules.detect: `plugins` array with a `voidPlugin()` call and no call to voidReact/voidVue/voidSvelte/voidSolid, when the `pages` option is true (opt-in because Pages mode is optional).
allowed:
// (options: { pages: true })
export default { plugins: [voidPlugin(), voidReact()] };
reported:
// (options: { pages: true })
export default { plugins: [voidPlugin(), voidMarkdown()] };
options: pages: boolean (default false): the app uses Pages routing
rules.partial: A lint cannot see whether pages/ exists; the option decides.

rules.name: prerender-satisfies-route-url
rules.summary: routing.prerender is annotated with `satisfies RouteUrl[]`.
rules.detect: `routing.prerender` ArrayExpression that is not wrapped in a TSSatisfiesExpression whose type is `RouteUrl[]`.
allowed: export default defineConfig({ routing: { typedRoutes: true, prerender: ['/'] satisfies RouteUrl[] } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ routing: { typedRoutes: true, prerender: ['/'] } });
rules.partial: Reported whenever the array literal is plain; the condition 'typedRoutes is on' (config/52) cannot be read from the same expression, so apps without typedRoutes get false reports.

rules.name: scandirs-keep-defaults
rules.summary: When inference.scanDirs is set it still lists every default directory the app uses, because it replaces the defaults.
rules.detect: In `inference.scanDirs` (array literal) report a missing entry for each of routes, pages, middleware, crons, queues, email, durable-objects, src that exists as a directory under the app root (an fs readdir of the root, not file contents).
allowed:
// void.config.ts   (root has routes/ and lib/)
export default defineConfig({ inference: { scanDirs: ['routes', 'lib'] } });
reported:
// void.config.ts   (root has routes/ and pages/)
export default defineConfig({ inference: { scanDirs: ['lib'] } });

// void.config.ts   (root has routes/)
export default defineConfig({ inference: { scanDirs: ['pages'] } });
rules.partial: Reads the directory listing of the app root; a dynamic scanDirs escapes.

rules.name: typed-routes-enabled
rules.summary: void.config.ts sets routing.typedRoutes: true.
rules.detect: The object passed to defineConfig has no `routing.typedRoutes` set to the literal `true` (missing routing, missing key, or false). Config assembled from spreads or variables is skipped.
allowed: export default defineConfig({ routing: { typedRoutes: true } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ routing: { typedRoutes: false } });
rules.partial: A recommendation: apps that do not want typed routes turn the rule off.

rules.name: void-plugin-in-vite-config
rules.summary: The Vite config includes voidPlugin() from 'void'.
rules.files: vite.config.* (and the framework configs nuxt.config.*, astro.config.* under vite.plugins)
rules.detect: The default-exported config (object, defineConfig(...) or arrow returning one) has a `plugins` array with no `voidPlugin()` call; an import of `voidPlugin` from a specifier other than 'void'. For nuxt.config.* and astro.config.* the array is `vite.plugins`. Plugin arrays built indirectly (spread, variable) are skipped.
allowed:
// vite.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [voidPlugin(), voidReact()] });
rules.partial: Merges the native-app, meta-framework and Nuxt/Astro forms of one requirement; analog.md shows voidPlugin() after analog(), so it is only an inclusion check, never an order check.

rules.name: void-plugin-options
rules.summary: voidPlugin() takes only persistTo and auxiliaryWorkers, and each auxiliaryWorkers entry only configPath, config, viteEnvironment and devOnly.
rules.detect: ObjectExpression argument of `voidPlugin(...)` with a key other than persistTo, auxiliaryWorkers; an ObjectExpression element of `auxiliaryWorkers` with a key other than configPath, config, viteEnvironment, devOnly.
rules.partial: Entries built outside the literal escape.

rules.name: void-plugin-root-config-only
rules.summary: voidPlugin() is called only in the root vite.config.ts (or the framework's root config), never in a generator's own config.
rules.detect: `voidPlugin()` call in a file that is not named vite.config.*, nuxt.config.*, astro.config.* or svelte.config.* at the app root.
rules.partial: A nested vite.config.* in a workspace package is the root of that package and is accepted.

rules.name: await-isr-revalidate
rules.summary: revalidate() from 'void/isr' is awaited or returned.
rules.detect: `revalidate(...)` (imported from 'void/isr') as an ExpressionStatement without `await`, and not returned.

rules.name: c-rewrite-usage
rules.summary: c.rewrite() gets a destination starting with '/', its result is returned, and the middleware skips already-rewritten paths.
rules.detect: (1) `c.rewrite(...)` (or `await c.rewrite(...)`) used as an ExpressionStatement, not returned. (2) A file with a `c.rewrite(...)` call and neither a `c.isRewritten()` call nor a read of `c.req.path` / `c.req.url` before it in the same function. (3) `c.rewrite(<string Literal or TemplateLiteral starting with a literal chunk>)` whose text does not begin with `/`.
rules.reports: the statement; the rewrite call; the argument
allowed: export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { if (c.req.path === '/a') return c.rewrite('/b'); await next(); });
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { if (c.isRewritten()) return next(); return c.rewrite('/b'); });
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { if (c.req.path !== '/a') return next(); return c.rewrite('/b'); });
reported: export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { c.rewrite('/b'); await next(); });
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { await c.rewrite('/b'); });
export default defineMiddleware(async (c, next) => { return c.rewrite('/maintenance'); });
rules.partial: Guards done in a helper escape.

rules.name: revalidate-header-value
rules.summary: x-revalidate is set with c.header('x-revalidate', '<whole-number seconds>'); 0 means do not cache.
rules.detect: `c.header('x-revalidate', v)` where v is a numeric Literal (the doc shows a string) or a string Literal that is not a non-negative integer.

rules.name: routing-fallbacks-spa-index
rules.summary: An SPA app does not add '/*': '/index.html' to routing.fallbacks; it already falls back there.
rules.detect: `routing.fallbacks` with key `/*` and value `/index.html`, when `inference.appType` is 'spa' in the same file or `settings.void.appType` is 'spa'.
allowed: export default defineConfig({ inference: { appType: 'spa' }, routing: { fallbacks: { '/app/*': '/app' } } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ inference: { appType: 'spa' }, routing: { fallbacks: { '/*': '/index.html' } } });
export default defineConfig({ inference: { appType: 'spa' }, routing: { fallbacks: { '/*': '/index.html', '/a': '/b' } } });
rules.partial: Without appType in the file the rule stays silent.

rules.name: routing-headers-cache-scope
rules.summary: A public or immutable Cache-Control rule does not cover signed-in pages, /api/auth/*, or every URL.
rules.detect: A `Cache-Control: ...` string under a `routing.headers` key that is `/*`, `/api/*`, `/api/auth/*` or `/*.html` and contains `public`, `s-maxage` or `immutable`.
allowed: export default defineConfig({ routing: { headers: { '/assets/*': ['Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable'] } } });
export default defineConfig({ routing: { headers: { '/*': ['X-Frame-Options: DENY'] } } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ routing: { headers: { '/*': ['Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600'] } } });
export default defineConfig({ routing: { headers: { '/*': ['Cache-Control: immutable'] } } });
rules.partial: Other patterns that happen to cover signed-in pages escape.

rules.name: routing-headers-shape
rules.summary: routing.headers maps '/'-prefixed patterns to arrays of 'Name: value' strings and carries no Set-Cookie or cookie-clearing Clear-Site-Data.
rules.detect: (1) Keys of `routing.headers` not starting with `/`; values that are not an ArrayExpression of string Literals matching /^[!#$%&'*+.^_`|~0-9A-Za-z-]+:\s*.+$/. (2) A string in a `routing.headers` array that starts with `Set-Cookie:` (case-insensitive), or starts with `Clear-Site-Data:` and contains `"cookies"` or `"*"`.
rules.reports: the key or the value; the string
allowed: export default defineConfig({ routing: { headers: { '/*': ['X-Frame-Options: DENY'] } } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ routing: { headers: { '/*': 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' } } });
export default defineConfig({ routing: { headers: { '/*': ['Set-Cookie: a=1'] } } });
rules.partial: Meaningful only on a Void platform.

rules.name: routing-option-values
rules.summary: routing.revalidate, routing.prerender and routing.notFound hold values of the documented shape.
rules.detect: (1) `routing.revalidate` whose value is a string Literal or an ObjectExpression with a non-numeric (or negative, non-integer) value. (2) `routing.prerender` that is not an ArrayExpression of string Literals, or has an element not starting with `/`. (3) `routing.notFound` string Literal outside those three.
rules.reports: the value; the element; the literal

rules.name: routing-redirects-shape
rules.summary: routing.redirects sources start with '/' or an https:// host, :splat needs a * source, and the status is one of 301, 302, 303, 307, 308.
rules.detect: (1) Keys of `routing.redirects` that do not start with '/' or 'https://'; an `http://` key; a key host containing `*` or a `:port`; an entry whose destination contains `:splat` while its key has no `*`. (2) Value of `routing.redirects` that is an object without `to`, or with a `status` literal outside {301,302,303,307,308}.
rules.reports: the key or the destination; the value
allowed: export default defineConfig({ routing: { redirects: { '/a': { to: '/b', status: 301 } } } });
reported: export default defineConfig({ routing: { redirects: { '/a': { to: '/b', status: 304 } } } });
export default defineConfig({ routing: { redirects: { '/a': { status: 301 } } } });
rules.partial: The `https://host` form is documented only for a literal host; wildcard hosts are reported.

rules.name: routing-rewrite-paths
rules.summary: Rewrite and fallback sources and destinations start with a single '/'; :splat needs a * source.
rules.detect: Keys and string values in `routing.rewrites` / `routing.fallbacks` not starting with `/` or starting with `//`; a `:splat` in a destination whose key has no `*`.
rules.partial: The single-slash rule is stated for runtime c.rewrite; the config form is assumed to match.

rules.name: routing-rules-order
rules.summary: In routing.redirects, rewrites and revalidate objects, specific patterns come before catch-alls; the first match wins.
rules.detect: An ObjectExpression for `routing.redirects`, `routing.rewrites` or `routing.revalidate` in which a key is matched by the glob (`*` matches any characters including `/`) of an earlier key; computed keys and spreads stop the check.
rules.partial: Rules from a `_redirects` file are not seen.

rules.name: email-test-harness

rules.detect: Import of 'vitest' (or 'vitest/*') when the nearest package.json lists `vite-plus` in dependencies or devDependencies.
rules.partial: Reads package.json.

rules.summary: Analog's vite.config.ts sets resolve.mainFields to ['module'].

rules.detect: Import of void/db, void/kv, void/storage or void/ai outside the exempt files.

rules.name: framework-compat-flags
rules.summary: Void apps on Analog, Nuxt and Astro enable nodejs_als (and nodejs_compat on Analog and Nuxt) in compatibility_flags.
rules.files: void.config.ts in an Analog, Nuxt or Astro project
rules.detect: `compatibility_flags` array literal found under `cloudflare` or `worker` (either place: the docs disagree where compatibility settings go) that lacks 'nodejs_als', or for Analog and Nuxt lacks 'nodejs_compat'. Reported on the array; with no array present nothing is reported.
allowed:
// (nuxt project) void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { compatibility_flags: ['nodejs_compat', 'nodejs_als'] } });

// (astro project) void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ worker: { compatibility_flags: ['nodejs_als'] } });
reported:
// (nuxt project) void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { compatibility_flags: ['nodejs_compat'] } });

// (astro project) void.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ cloudflare: { compatibility_flags: [] } });
rules.partial: Accepts either location on purpose; a config that sets no flags at all is not reported because the placement is disputed.

rules.name: nitro-config
rules.summary: Nitro-based apps (Analog, Nuxt) set the cloudflare-module preset and list void/nitro in nitro.modules.
rules.detect: (1) The nitro object (`nitro` in nuxt.config, or the `nitro` option of `analog({...})`) has no `preset: 'cloudflare-module'`. (2) `nitro.modules` array literal lacking 'void/nitro'; for Analog also lacking 'nitro-cloudflare-dev', or the analog options lacking `ssr: true`.
rules.reports: the nitro object; the modules array
allowed:
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({ nitro: { preset: 'cloudflare-module' } });

// vite.config.ts
export default { plugins: [analog({ nitro: { preset: 'cloudflare-module' } })] };

// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({ nitro: { modules: ['void/nitro'] } });

// vite.config.ts
export default { plugins: [analog({ ssr: true, nitro: { modules: ['nitro-cloudflare-dev', 'void/nitro'] } })] };
reported:
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({ nitro: { preset: 'node' } });

// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({ nitro: { modules: [] } });

// vite.config.ts
export default { plugins: [analog({ nitro: { modules: ['nitro-cloudflare-dev'] } })] };
rules.partial: voidPlugin() in the plugins array is checked by void-plugin-in-vite-config.

rules.name: no-cloudflare-vite-plugin-with-void
rules.summary: React Router and TanStack Start configs do not add a separate Cloudflare Vite plugin next to voidPlugin().
rules.detect: Import of '@cloudflare/vite-plugin' (or a `cloudflare()` plugin call) in a config that also calls voidPlugin().
allowed:
import { voidPlugin } from 'void';
export default { plugins: [voidPlugin(), reactRouter()] };
reported:
import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin';
export default { plugins: [voidPlugin(), cloudflare(), reactRouter()] };

import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin';
export default { plugins: [cloudflare(), voidPlugin(), tanstackStart()] };

rules.name: react-router-void-in-loaders-only
rules.summary: In React Router, void/* helpers and void/env secrets are used in loaders and actions (or a .server module), not in route components.
rules.files: app/routes/** files that default-export a component
rules.detect: References to bindings imported from void/db, void/kv, void/storage, void/ai, or `env.<NAME>` (NAME not VITE_) from void/env, inside the default-exported component (or functions it contains), in a file that also exports a component.

rules.name: sveltekit-no-void-in-client
rules.summary: In SvelteKit, void/* helpers are used only in server load functions, actions and API routes (+page.server.ts, +server.ts), not in .svelte files or universal +page.ts / +layout.ts.
rules.detect: Import of void/db, void/kv, void/storage, void/ai, void/auth or void/sandbox in those files.

rules.name: tanstack-void-in-server-fn
rules.summary: In TanStack Start, void/* runtime helpers are used only inside server functions (createServerFn handlers), never in browser code.
rules.files: routes and components in a TanStack Start project (files that export a React component)

allowed:
const getUsers = createServerFn().handler(async () => db.query.users.findMany());
export default function P() { return null; }
export default function P() { return null; }
reported:
export const Route = createFileRoute('/')({ loader: () => db.query.users.findMany() });
export default function P() { return null; }
export default function P() { const x = kv.get('a'); return null; }
rules.partial: Needs scope analysis. Server-only helper modules (no component export) are not checked.

rules.name: void-plugin-before-framework-plugin
rules.summary: In React Router and TanStack Start configs, voidPlugin() comes before the framework plugin.
